'''Robert Taylor III''' (born December 28, 1973) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[cornerback]] for 10 seasons in the [[National Football League]] (NFL).  He played [[college football]] for the [[Notre Dame Fighting Irish football|Notre Dame Fighting Irish]], earning consensus [[College Football All-America Team|All-American]] honors. He was selected in the second round of the [[1995 NFL draft]] by the [[Philadelphia Eagles]]. He also played for the [[Seattle Seahawks]].

==Early life==
Taylor was born in [[Houston]], Texas.<ref name="nflprofile">National Football League, Historical Players, [http://www.nfl.com/player/bobbytaylor/2503252/profile Bobby Taylor]. Retrieved February 7, 2012.</ref> He attended [[Longview High School]] in [[Longview, Texas]],<ref name="dbfprofile">databaseFootball.com, Players, {{usurped|1=[https://web.archive.org/web/20120326212122/http://www.databasefootball.com/players/playerpage.htm?ilkid=TAYLOBOB02 Bobby Taylor]}}. Retrieved February 7, 2012.</ref> and played [[high school football]] for the Longview Lobos and was also a member of the Lobos' Texas Class 5A state basketball championship team.  In addition to playing for the Lobos 1992 Basketball State Championship Team; Taylor was a three-year starter for the Lobos in football he ran a leg on the state champion 1,600-meter relay squad.  He was inducted into the Texas High School Football Hall of Fame's 2012 class.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Staff Reports |date=January 20, 2012 |title=Ex-Lobo Bobby Taylor to be inducted in Texas High School Football Hall of Fame |work=Longview News Journal |url=https://www.news-journal.com/news/local/ex-lobo-bobby-taylor-to-be-inducted-in-texas-high/article_75d3f88f-b390-5556-9aec-1b1b1ebea207.html}}</ref> Taylor was a two-time Class 5A all-state pick for football, and named to the first-team defense on the UIL all-century team in 2009.  These accolades earned him as the first player in Longview Lobo history to have his jersey, No. 24, retired.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Orts |first=Jason |date=May 19, 2012 |title=Hall of Fame profile: Longview's triple threat an East Texas legend |work=Waco Tribune-Herald |url=http://www.wacotrib.com/sports/hall-of-fame-profile-longview-s-triple-threat-an-east/article_0ce98753-7f55-59a4-b7ca-4d155ecab57e.html |access-date=April 6, 2018}}</ref>

==College career==
Taylor attended the [[University of Notre Dame]], where he played for the [[Notre Dame Fighting Irish football]] team from 1992 to 1994.  As a Junior in 1994, was recognized as a consensus first-team All-American.<ref>''2010 Division I Football Record Book'', [http://fs.ncaa.org/Docs/stats/football_records/DI/2010/Awards.pdf Award Winners and All-Americans], National Collegiate Athletic Association, Indianapolis, Indiana, p. 10 (2010). Retrieved February 7, 2012.</ref>

'''Charles Lee "Boobie" Clark''' (November 8, 1949{{spaced ndash}}October 25, 1988) was a professional [[American football]] [[running back]] who played in the [[National Football League]] (NFL) for eight seasons and was named the [[UPI AFL-AFC Rookie of the Year|UPI AFL–AFC Rookie of the Year]] for 1973.<ref name=TOP />

==Early life==
Clark was born in [[Jacksonville, Florida]] and was an athletic standout at [[Stanton College Preparatory School|Stanton High School]], where the nickname "Boobie" originated. He played [[tight end]] in high school and at [[Bethune-Cookman University]].<ref name=TOP>[http://jacksonville.com/special/athletes_of_century/stories/37.shtml "#37 Charles "Boobie" Clark/Football"] Florida Times-Union, 2000AD Top 100 Athletes</ref>

He was an offensive line stalwart at Bethune-Cookman, with one exception. During a 48–0 victory over [[Albany State University]] in 1971, head coach Cy McClairen placed Clark at fullback because a lot of his teammates were nursing injuries.

That game film was sent to [[Cincinnati Bengals]] head coach [[Paul Brown]] to showcase other players, but Brown saw something in Clark and decided he would draft him if the opportunity came.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://bcuathletics.com/news/2013/8/22/_bcutbt_boobie_clark.aspx|title=#BCUTBT: "Boobie" Clark|website=Bcuathletics.com|date=August 22, 2013 |access-date=20 November 2021}}</ref>

==Professional career==
He was drafted in the 12th round of the [[1973 NFL draft]] by the Cincinnati Bengals and became a fullback. Despite inexperience at the position, he was a breakout star with 988 yards in 254 carries (a 3.9 average) and eight touchdowns and 45 receptions for 347 yards (a 7.7 average). He was named [[American Football Conference]] Rookie of the Year in 1973.<ref name="pro-football-reference.com">{{Cite web|url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/C/ClarBo00.htm|title=Boobie Clark Stats|website=Pro-Football-Reference.com|access-date=20 November 2021}}</ref>

That same year, Clark was involved in an on-field incident in which he struck [[Dale Hackbart]] of the [[Denver Broncos]] with a right forearm to the back of Hackbart's head and neck after a play was finished. Hackbart filed a lawsuit and the case eventually went to trial as an [[intentional tort]], specifically [[battery (tort)]]. Clark testified that his team was losing and that he intentionally hit Hackbart due to his frustration. The case went as far as the [[United States Court of Appeals for the Tenth Circuit|United States Court of Appeals (10th Circuit)]] in 1979.<ref>{{Cite journal|url=https://openjurist.org/601/f2d/516/hackbart-v-cincinnati-bengals-inc|title=601 F2d 516 Hackbart v. Cincinnati Bengals Inc|first1=United States Court of|last1=Appeals|first2=Tenth|last2=Circuit|date=20 November 1979|volume=F2d|issue=601|pages=516|access-date=20 November 2021|website=Openjurist.org}}</ref>

In 1974, Clark was limited to eight games, with 312 yards in 99 attempts (a 3.2 average) with five touchdowns and 23 receptions for 194 yards (an 8.4 average).

A year later, 1975, he bounced back played all 14 games with 594 yards on 167 attempts (a 3.6 average) and four touchdowns plus 42 receptions for 334 yards (an 8.0 average).

In 1976, Clark gained 671 yards on 151 attempts (a 4.4 average) and seven touchdowns with 23 receptions for 158 yards (a 6.9 average) and one touchdown.

In 1977, he was limited to 10 games with 226 yards on 68 attempts (a 3.3 average) and one touchdown with seven receptions for 33 yards (a 4.7 average).

Clark's sixth and final season with the Bengals was 1978. He played in 14 games and rushed for 187 yards on 40 attempts (a career-high 4.7 average) and caught 11 passes for 43 yards (a 6.6 average).<ref name="pro-football-reference.com"/>

For his six seasons with the Bengals, Clark rushed for 2,978 yards and 25 touchdowns. He also caught 151 passes for 1,139 yards and two touchdowns.

Clark was traded to the [[History of the Tennessee Titans|Houston Oilers]] prior to the 1979 season, the first of two with the Oilers. In 1979, he rushed for 51 yards on 22 carries (a 2.3 average) and had six receptions for 58 yards. The 1980 season would be his last, when he had just one carry for three yards. He retired prior to the 1981 season.

==After football==
Clark died of a blood clot in his lung at the age of 38 on October 25, 1988, at Memorial Hospital in [[Jacksonville, Florida]].<ref>[https://www.nytimes.com/1988/10/26/obituaries/booby-clark-football-player-37.html?pagewanted=1    Booby Clark, Football Player, 37], ''[[The New York Times]]'', October 26, 1988</ref>

The City of Jacksonville renamed Sherwood Forest Playground as Charles "Boobie" Clark Park and Pool in his honor.<ref>[http://apps2.coj.net/parksinternet/parkdetails.asp?parkid=49 "Charles Boobie Clark Park and Pool"] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120214045415/http://apps2.coj.net/parksinternet/parkdetails.asp?parkid=49 |date=2012-02-14 }} City of Jacksonville website, Parks & Recreation</ref> In 2000, the [[Florida Times-Union]] named Clark number 37 on their list of the top 100 athletes from Jacksonville.<ref name=TOP/>

In 2001, he was posthumously inducted into the Bethune-Cookman University Athletic Hall of Fame.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.bcuathletics.com/ViewArticle.dbml?DB_OEM_ID%3D23910%26ATCLID%3D205680634 |title=Archived copy |access-date=2014-01-27 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20140203012118/http://www.bcuathletics.com/ViewArticle.dbml?DB_OEM_ID=23910&ATCLID=205680634 |archivedate=2014-02-03 }}</ref>

'''Robert Earl Walden''' (March 9, 1938 – August 27, 2018)<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.thepostsearchlight.com/2018/09/04/bainbridge-resident-bobby-waldens-passing-inspires-look-into-storied-football-career/ |title=Bainbridge resident Bobby Walden's passing inspires look into storied football career |date=2018-09-04 |website=The Post-Searchlight |language=en-US |access-date=2018-10-14}}</ref> was an American professional [[gridiron football|football]] player who was a [[Punter (football position)|punter]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL) and [[Canadian Football League]] (CFL). Walden played for 17 seasons, 14 of which were played in the NFL from 1964 to 1977. Previously, Walden had played three years in the CFL from 1961 to 1963. Walden was a part of the [[Pittsburgh Steelers]]' [[Super Bowl IX]] and [[Super Bowl X]] winning teams.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://bainbridgega.com/news/publish/1101walden.shtml |title=Walden: Steeler All-Time Great |publisher=bainbridgega.com |date=November 2, 2007 |access-date=August 7, 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120316104349/http://bainbridgega.com/news/publish/1101walden.shtml |archive-date=March 16, 2012 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

He led the NFL in punting in 1964 with a 46.4 yard average and was selected to the [[Pro Bowl]] after the 1969 season.

Before his NFL career, Walden led the CFL in punting, rushing, and receiving as a member of the [[Edmonton Eskimos]] in 1961 and 1962.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/201015-the-almost-all-time-pittsburgh-steelers-offense#/articles/201015-the-almost-all-time-pittsburgh-steelers-offense |title=The Almost All-Time Pittsburgh Steelers Offense |publisher=bleacherreport.com |date=June 17, 2009 |access-date=August 7, 2011 }}</ref>

Walden played for the University of Georgia Bulldogs for three years from 1958 to 1960. In 1958, as a sophomore, he led the nation in average yards per punt. In 1960, he set an Orange Bowl record for yards per punt.

===New Orleans Saints===
Williams was signed as an [[undrafted free agent]] by the [[New Orleans Saints]] on April 26, 2001 and soon began a conversion to the [[tight end]] position.  Waived in September, then signed off the [[practice squad]] on October 27, he played in his first NFL game October 28 and made his first start the following week.  He finished his first NFL season with 20 receptions for 202 yards and 3 touchdowns.<ref name="saints bio" />

Williams was the top pass-catching tight end for the Saints in 2002 with 13 receptions for 143 yards and 2 touchdowns.<ref name="saints bio" />  The following year he set career highs with 41 catches for 436 yards and 5 touchdowns, leading the [[National Football Conference|NFC]] in touchdowns among tight ends.<ref name="saints bio" />  In 2004 Williams started a career-high 8 games.<ref name="saints bio" />

Williams tore the [[Anterior cruciate ligament|ACL]] and [[Medial collateral ligament|MCL]] in his right knee during a 2005 preseason game and did not play the entire year.  He was released by the Saints in February 2006.<ref name="espn giants">{{cite news|last1=Pasquarelli|first1=Len|title=Giants sign former Saints TE Boo Williams|url=http://www.espn.com/nfl/news/story?id=2475912|accessdate=June 14, 2016|work=ESPN|date=June 8, 2006}}</ref>

===New York Giants===
Williams was signed by the [[New York Giants]] in June 2006 but waived before the regular season began.<ref name="espn giants" /><ref>{{cite web|title=Boo Williams - Tight End|url=http://www.rotoworld.com/player/nfl/1044/boo-williams|website=Rotoworld|accessdate=June 14, 2016}}</ref>

===Kansas City Brigade===
On January 19, 2007, Williams signed with the [[Kansas City Brigade]] of the [[Arena Football League (1987–2008)|Arena Football League]].  On March 3, 2008, he was placed on recallable waivers by the Brigade.<ref>{{cite web|title=Kansas City Brigade|url=http://www.arenafan.com/teams/?page=transactions&type=old&team=115|website=ArenaFan.com|accessdate=April 30, 2018}}</ref>

==Life after football==
Williams struggled with a multitude of depression, anger, and anxiety issues after retiring from football, the cause of which he attributes to head trauma sustained during his NFL career.  After nearly taking his own life in 2011, Williams spent four months at the Crosby Center in San Diego for diagnosis and treatment of the problems he was suffering from.  Williams later worked with the Crosby Center to help other NFL players dealing with similar issues post-retirement.<ref>{{cite news|last1=Rousseau|first1=Randi|title=Former Saints player becomes advocate for mental health after NFL run|url=http://www.wdsu.com/article/former-saints-player-becomes-advocate-for-mental-health-after-nfl-run-1/3374030|accessdate=June 15, 2016|work=WDSU 6 News|date=November 24, 2014}}</ref><ref name="nol mag">{{cite news|last1=Patch|first1=Lianna|title=After the Game Ends|url=http://www.livingneworleans.com/?p=10972|accessdate=June 15, 2016|work=New Orleans Living Magazine|date=January 2, 2015}}</ref>

Williams uses [[cannabis (drug)|cannabis]] to treat the chronic pain and neurological problems that have resulted from his football career.<ref name="vice">{{cite news|last1=Davis|first1=David|title=After The NFL, Pot Saved Boo Williams' Life. He's Trying To Return The Favor.|url=https://www.vice.com/en/article/after-the-nfl-pot-saved-boo-williams-life-hes-trying-to-return-the-favor/|access-date=April 29, 2018|work=Vice Sports|date=November 3, 2016}}</ref>  As a member of the Gridiron Cannabis Coalition he has been active in speaking about his experience using cannabis as medicine and advocating for the NFL to change its policy.<ref>{{cite news|last1=Downs|first1=David|title=Former NFL players end-run federal marijuana research blockade|url=https://blog.sfgate.com/smellthetruth/2016/04/08/former-nfl-players-try-to-sack-federal-marijuana-research-blockade/|accessdate=April 29, 2018|work=Smell the Truth|publisher=San Francisco Chronicle|date=April 8, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160819080226/https://blog.sfgate.com/smellthetruth/2016/04/08/former-nfl-players-try-to-sack-federal-marijuana-research-blockade/|archive-date=August 19, 2016|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|last1=Black|first1=Bobby|title=Changing the game -- A high-profile San Diege resident, Boo williams is a former NFL star turned cannabis advocate and entrepreneur on a mission.|url=https://issuu.com/sensimediagroup/docs/feb_2018_san_diego_sensi/30|accessdate=April 29, 2018|work=Sensi Magazine|issue=February 2018}}</ref>

Williams founded the Boo Williams Athletic Academy, an after-school program providing academic and athletic activities for children to engage in.<ref name="nol mag" />  He has also worked as a [[bounty hunter]] and appeared in two episodes of the reality TV show [[Dog and Beth: On the Hunt]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Boo Williams|url=https://www.imdb.com/name/nm2473263/?ref_=ttfc_fc_cl_t25|website=IMDb|accessdate=June 15, 2016}}</ref>

'''Robert Benson Scott''' (born April 2, 1949) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[quarterback]] for 10 seasons in the [[National Football League]] (NFL) for the [[New Orleans Saints]] from 1973 to 1981.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Bobby Scott Stats, Height, Weight, Position, Draft, College |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/S/ScotBo00.htm |access-date=March 16, 2024 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> He later played for the [[New Jersey Generals]] and [[Chicago Blitz]] of the [[United States Football League]] (USFL) in 1983.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Shearer |first=John  |date=November 26, 2020 |title=Former Rossville Quarterback Bobby Scott Recalls His UT Glory Days |url=https://www.chattanoogan.com/2020/11/26/419031/John-Shearer-Former-Rossville.aspx |access-date=March 16, 2024 |website=Chattanoogan.com |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Robert Scott football statistics |url=https://www.statscrew.com/football/stats/p-scottbob002 |access-date=March 16, 2024 |website=StatsCrew.com |language=en}}</ref> He graduated from Rossville High School in [[Rossville, Georgia]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Crawley |first=Stan |date=May 21, 2006 |title=Bobby Scott Will Be Inducted Into Greater Knoxville Sports Hall Of Fame |url=https://www.chattanoogan.com/2006/5/21/86212/Bobby-Scott-Will-Be-Inducted-Into.aspx |access-date=March 16, 2024 |website=Chattanoogan.com |language=en}}</ref> He was second on the Saints depth chart behind [[Archie Manning]]. In 1976, Manning had surgery on his throwing shoulder and Scott had the opportunity to start.<ref name="s480">{{cite web | title=Manning Operated On | website=The New York Times | date=1976-02-03 | url=https://www.nytimes.com/1976/02/03/archives/manning-operated-on.html | access-date=2025-01-08}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Bobby Scott 1976 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/S/ScotBo00/gamelog/1976/ |access-date=2025-01-08 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref>

He played [[college football]] for the [[Tennessee Volunteers football|Tennessee Volunteers]], earning  Most Outstanding Player honors in the 1971 [[Sugar Bowl]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Bobby Scott - Sugar Bowl Hall of Fame |url=https://allstatesugarbowl.org/sports/2023/11/28/bobby-scott.aspx |access-date=March 16, 2024 |website=Sugar Bowl |language=en}}</ref> Tennessee defeated the [[Air Force Academy]] Falcons 34–13 in the game.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Backus |first=Will |date=December 24, 2019 |title=How Tennessee Vols football has fared in every bowl game it has played |url=https://www.knoxnews.com/story/sports/college/university-of-tennessee/football/2019/12/24/tennessee-football-bowl-history-ut-vols/4390569002/ |access-date=March 16, 2024 |website=[[Knoxville News Sentinel]] |language=en-US}}</ref>

Shaw II''' (born April 23, 1975) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[wide receiver]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL).{{Cite web|url=http://www.espn.com/nfl/player/stats/_/id/1558/bobby-shaw|title=Bobby Shaw|website=ESPN.com|access-date=2018-08-18}} He played [[college football]] for the [[California Golden Bears football|California Golden Bears]], earning third-team [[College Football All-America Team|All-American]] honors in 1997. Shaw played for five NFL teams: [[Seattle Seahawks]], [[Pittsburgh Steelers]], [[Jacksonville Jaguars]], [[Buffalo Bills]], and [[San Diego Chargers]].{{Cite news|url=https://www.mercurynews.com/2016/03/05/concussions-former-nfl-players-sound-off-on-head-injuries-during-east-bay-school-forum/|title=Concussions: Former NFL players sound off on head injuries during East Bay school forum|date=2016-03-05|work=The Mercury News|access-date=2018-08-18|language=en-US}} Shaw attended [[Galileo Academy of Science and Technology|Galileo High School]] and attended the [[University of California, Berkeley]].{{Cite news|url=http://www.sfexaminer.com/galileo-high-school-to-unveil-sports-hall-of-fame/|title=Galileo High School to unveil sports Hall of Fame|work=The San Francisco Examiner|access-date=2018-08-18|language=en-US|archive-date=2018-08-18|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180818083918/http://www.sfexaminer.com/galileo-high-school-to-unveil-sports-hall-of-fame/|url-status=dead}} He graduated from Cal as the school's all-time leader in [[reception (gridiron football)|receptions]] with 180 catches for 2,731 yards and 27 [[touchdown]]s.{{Cite news|url=https://www.californiagoldenblogs.com/2014/5/17/5722800/cgb-hall-of-fame-8-thomas-decoud-vs-9-bobby-shaw|title=CGB Hall of Fame: Thomas DeCoud vs. Bobby Shaw|work=California Golden Blogs|access-date=2018-08-18}} In 1996, [[Steve Mariucci]] became the Golden Bears' head coach. Shaw prospered under Mariucci, with 12 catches for 168 yards in a game against [[UCLA Bruins football|UCLA]] and three touchdowns scores in a 48-42 triple-overtime win over Oregon State. In the Aloha Bowl following that season, Shaw scored twice on passes from Pat Barnes in Cal's 42–38 loss to Navy. Shaw was named first-team All-Pac-10 for his performance that year. In 1997, Shaw became captain on [[Tom Holmoe]]'s first team. He set single-season records with 74 receptions for 1,093 yards and 11 touchdowns. It was a tough year for Cal, but Shaw helped deliver one of the Bears' three wins with 158 yards and 2 touchdowns in a 40–36 win over Oklahoma. He was again voted to the All-Pac-10 first team, and became the third Cal wide receiver to win first-team All-America honors from Sporting News. UCLA Head Coach Bob Toledo had stated "(he's) the best receiver in the conference, one of the best in the country, and he'll end up being the best receiver in Cal history." Shaw was selected in the sixth round of the [[1998 NFL draft]] by the [[Seattle Seahawks]].{{Cite web |title=1998 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/1998/draft.htm |access-date=2023-03-29 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}} He signed later that year with the Pittsburgh Steelers, and played six years with the Steelers, Jaguars, Bills, and Chargers.{{Cite web|url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/S/ShawBo00.htm|title=Bobby Shaw Stats|website=Pro-Football-Reference.com|access-date=2020-07-15}} He currently resides in California. == References == {{Seahawks1998DraftPicks}} {{DEFAULTSORT:Shaw, Bobby}} [[Category:1975 births]] [[Category:Living people]] [[Category:Players of American football from San Francisco]] [[Category:American football wide receivers]] [[Category:California Golden Bears football players]] [[Category:Seattle Seahawks players]] [[Category:Pittsburgh Steelers players]] [[Category:Jacksonville Jaguars players]] [[Category:Buffalo Bills players]] [[Category:San Diego Chargers players]] [[Category:21st-century American sportsmen]] [[Category:21st-century African-American sportsmen]] [[Category:20th-century American sportsmen]] [[Category:20th-century African-American sportsmen]]

([[North Miami Beach, Florida]]) |college=[[Cal State Fullerton Titans football|Cal State Fullerton]] |draftyear=1981 |draftround=8 |draftpick=202 |pastteams= * [[Cincinnati Bengals]] ({{NFL Year|1981|1986}}) * [[Tampa Bay Buccaneers]] ({{NFL Year|1987}}) |statlabel1=[[Interception]]s |statvalue1=10 |statlabel2=[[Fumble]] recoveries |statvalue2=2 |statlabel3=[[Quarterback sack|Sacks]] |statvalue3=4.0 |pfr=KempBo20 }} '''Bobby Kemp''' (May 29, 1959 – February 7, 1998) was an American professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[Safety (gridiron football position)|safety]] for seven seasons with the [[Cincinnati Bengals]] and [[Tampa Bay Buccaneers]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Cal State Fullerton Titans football|Cal State Fullerton Titans]]. ==College career== After attending [[Taft College]], a junior college in [[Taft, California]], he played [[college football]] at [[California State University, Fullerton]] for two seasons, with five interceptions his junior year (1979) and three his senior year (1980).{{Cite web|url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/players/bobby-kemp-1.html|title = Bobby Kemp College Stats}} He was selected by the Bengals in the eighth round of the [[1981 NFL draft]].{{Cite web|url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/K/KempBo20.htm|title = Bobby Kemp Stats|website = [[Pro-Football-Reference.com]]}} ==Professional career== During his rookie season (1981), Kemp was the starting strong safety as the Bengals defeated the [[San Diego Chargers]] in the coldest game in NFL history, the AFC Championship Game dubbed the "[[Freezer Bowl]]" on January 10, 1982. With the Bengals holding a 17–7 lead and the Chargers offense driving late in the first half, Kemp intercepted a [[Dan Fouts]] pass to [[Kellen Winslow]] to thwart the drive. The Bengals went on to win, 27–7.{{Cite web|url=http://news.cincinnati.com/article/20131231/SPT02/312310085/An-oral-history-Freezer-Bowl|title = Cincinnati News, Sports and Things to do | Cincinnati Enquirer}} The win propelled the Bengals to [[Super Bowl XVI]], which they lost, 26–21, to the [[San Francisco 49ers]]. Kemp was the Bengals starter at strong safety in that game.{{Cite web|url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/198201240cin.htm|title = Super Bowl XVI - San Francisco 49ers vs. Cincinnati Bengals - January 24th, 1982|website = [[Pro-Football-Reference.com]]}} During his seven seasons as a [[strong safety]] and [[free safety]] with the Bengals, he played in 83 games, starting 69 of those. In 1983, he had three interceptions, and a career-best four in 1984. His last year in the NFL was in 1987 for the Buccaneers, for whom he started and played in 12 games as a strong safety with one interception.{{Cite web|url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/K/KempBo20.htm|title = Bobby Kemp Stats|website = [[Pro-Football-Reference.com]]}} ==Personal life and death== Kemp later became a paramedic in [[Glendale, California]], after retiring from football due to knee problems. He met his first wife, Christy, when they were students at Taft College. They were married for 13 years. On February 7, 1998, Kemp committed suicide in his [[North Hollywood, California]] home.{{Cite web|url=https://www.si.com/2015/07/02/nfl-cincinnati-bengals-1986|title=One Team, 25 Years on}} He was 38. He was survived by his second wife, Inga, and their two-year-old daughter. {{cite web | url = https://vault.si.com/vault/2011/12/12/a-different-kind-of-pain | title = A different kind of pain | last = Gagne | first = Mark | date = Dec 12, 2011 | website = [[Sports Illustrated]] | access-date = May 9, 2023 }} ==References== {{Reflist}} {{Bengals1981DraftPicks}} {{DEFAULTSORT:Kemp, Bobby}} [[Category:1959 births]] [[Category:1998 deaths]] [[Category:1998 suicides]] [[Category:American football safeties]] [[Category:Cal State Fullerton Titans football players]] [[Category:Cincinnati Bengals players]] [[Category:Tampa Bay Buccaneers players]] [[Category:California State University, Fullerton, alumni]] [[Category:Players of American football from Oakland, California]] [[Category:People from Taft, California]] [[Category:Players of American football from Kern County, California]] [[Category:Players of American football from Glendale, California]] [[Category:Suicides in California]] [[Category:20th-century American sportsmen]]

'''Booker Thomas Moore''' (June 23, 1959{{spaced ndash}}September 20, 2009) was an American professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[running back]] for the [[Buffalo Bills]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL).

Moore set six high school records in football while attending [[Flint Southwestern Academy]] in [[Flint, Michigan]].<ref name="obit">{{Cite web |last=Mickle |first=Bryn |date=September 21, 2009 |title=Former Flint Southwestern standout Booker Moore dies |url=http://www.mlive.com/news/flint/index.ssf/2009/09/former_flint_southwestern_stan.html |access-date=November 17, 2023 |website=[[Mlive.com|Michigan Live]]}}</ref> As a member of the [[Penn State Nittany Lions football|Penn State Nittany Lions]], Moore rushed for 2,072 yards and 20 touchdowns from 1977 to 1980,<ref name="PSUtotals">{{Cite web |last=Kline |first=Bill |date=September 21, 2009 |title=Former Lion Standout Booker Moore Dies |url=https://blogs.mcall.com/nittany_lines/2009/09/former-lion-standout-booker-moore-dies.html |access-date=2025-06-29 |newspaper=[[The Morning Call]]}}</ref> and played for a [[NCAA Division I FBS National Football Championship|national championship]] in the [[1979 Sugar Bowl]] versus [[Alabama Crimson Tide football|Alabama]].<ref name="obit" />

Moore was selected in the first round by the [[Buffalo Bills]] in the [[1981 NFL draft]]. He played four seasons for the Bills, appearing in 51 games from 1982 to 1985. Moore did not start in his rookie season, but he did manage to rush for 38 yards on 16 attempts. In his second season he started 11 games for the Bills. In a 28–23 loss to the [[Baltimore Colts]] Moore rushed for 53 yards on 12 attempts, taking over for starter [[Roosevelt Leaks]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Baltimore Colts at Buffalo Bills - September 18th, 1983 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/198309180buf.htm |access-date=November 17, 2023 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> Though he would start 15 games the next season, his production went down, only getting 84 yards on 24 attempts. He would not score a rushing touchdown until 1985, his final season. His touchdown was the lone score for Buffalo in 17–7 loss to the [[Cleveland Browns]]. Moore had scored the go-ahead touchdown in the first half, but the Bills defense allowed 10 unanswered points, including an 11-yard pass from [[Bernie Kosar]] to [[Ozzie Newsome]] in the fourth quarter that sealed the game.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Buffalo Bills at Cleveland Browns - November 17th, 1985 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/198511170cle.htm |access-date=November 17, 2023 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Booker Moore Stats, Height, Weight, Position, Draft, College |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/M/MoorBo00.htm |access-date=November 17, 2023 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> He was diagnosed with [[Guillain–Barré syndrome]] shortly after being drafted.

Upon retirement in 1986, Moore became a [[Genesee County, Michigan]], sheriff's deputy.<ref name="obit" /> He died of a [[Myocardial infarction|heart attack]] at his home in Flint on September 20, 2009.<ref name="obit" />

'''Robert J. Morse''' (born October 3, 1965) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[running back]] and [[return specialist]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL) for the [[Philadelphia Eagles]], [[San Francisco 49ers]], and [[New Orleans Saints]]. He played [[college football]] for the [[Michigan State Spartans football|Michigan State Spartans]]. Morse was selected by the Eagles in the 12th round of the [[1987 NFL draft]]<ref>{{Cite web |title=1987 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/1987/draft.htm |access-date=2023-10-01 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> but was placed on reserve status in April 1988 and did not play football for the remainder of that year. He was traded to the Saints in 1989 and was on and off the roster several times during the year. He was signed by the San Francisco 49ers for five days in November 1989 but did not play in a regular season game before re-signing, and finishing his career, with the Saints.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Bobby Morse NFL Transactions |url= https://www.profootballarchives.com/transactionsm/mors00200.html |access-date=2023-11-04|website=profootballarchives.com|language=en}}</ref>

'''Bobby Gene Rainey, Jr.''' (born October 16, 1987) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[running back]] and [[return specialist]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Western Kentucky Hilltoppers football|Western Kentucky Hilltoppers]], earning second-team [[College Football All-America Team|All-American]] honors in 2011. Rainey signed with the [[Baltimore Ravens]] as an [[undrafted free agent]] after the [[2012 NFL draft]]. He also played for the [[Cleveland Browns]], the [[Tampa Bay Buccaneers]] and the [[New York Giants]].

==College career==
In 2011, Rainey had 1,695 rushing yards and 17 total touchdowns while playing running back at [[Western Kentucky Hilltoppers football|Western Kentucky University]].<ref>[http://www.wkusports.com/ViewArticle.dbml?DB_OEM_ID=5400&ATCLID=1566163 Player file] {{webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100928204830/http://www.wkusports.com/ViewArticle.dbml?DB_OEM_ID=5400&ATCLID=1566163 |date=September 28, 2010 }} WKU Sports</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/player/stats/_/id/15501/bobby-rainey|title=Bobby Rainey Jr. Stats|website=ESPN.com|access-date=December 6, 2021}}</ref> In 2010, Rainey was one of the top rushers in College Football. He led the nation in rushing attempts (340) and was third in the nation in rushing yards (1649). He was named the Sun Belt Conference Offensive Player of the Year in 2010 as well as earning All-American honors from SI.com.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/2010/football/ncaa/12/14/all-american-team/index.html |title=Cam Newton, Nick Fairley headline SI.com's 2010 All-Americas - NCAA Football - SI.com |access-date=July 7, 2011 |archive-date=December 2, 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131202223906/http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/2010/football/ncaa/12/14/all-american-team/index.html |url-status=dead }}</ref> In July 2011, he was named to the Maxwell Award Watch List.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.maxwellfootballclub.org/news/11-07-05/2011_Maxwell_Award_Watch_List.aspx |title=Football Club News | Maxwell Football Club |access-date=July 7, 2011 |archive-date=August 10, 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110810100717/http://www.maxwellfootballclub.org/news/11-07-05/2011_Maxwell_Award_Watch_List.aspx |url-status=dead }}</ref> In August, he was named to the Doak Walker Award Watch list.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://smu.edu/doakwalker/doak_candidates.asp |title=Doak Walker Award |access-date=August 12, 2009 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081230155145/http://smu.edu/doakwalker/doak_candidates.asp |archive-date=December 30, 2008 }} Doak Walker Award</ref> In 2009, he totaled over 2,100 yards and gained notoriety as one of the premier Kick Returners in College Football. His two official forty yard dash times were 4.42 and 4.45 respectively. He was also a member of the Western Kentucky Track & Field team.

===School records===
Rainey holds school records for WKU in rushing yards in a season (1,695) and rushing yards in a career (4,523). He is just the eighth [[Division I (NCAA)#Football Bowl Subdivision|FBS]] player since 2000 to rack up back-to-back 1,500-yard seasons. That list includes [[LaDainian Tomlinson]] (TCU), [[Ray Rice]] (Rutgers), [[Steven Jackson]] (Oregon State), [[DeAngelo Williams]] (Memphis), and [[Darren McFadden]] (Arkansas).

==Professional career==
===Baltimore Ravens===
Rainey signed with the [[Baltimore Ravens]] as an undrafted free agent. On September 10, 2012, he was released by the Ravens. On September 12, he was re-signed to the practice squad and became practice squad captain. On October 16, Rainey was promoted to the active roster after the team placed [[Lardarius Webb]] on injured reserve.<ref>{{cite web | title= Ravens promote Rainey to active roster, Webb placed on IR | work= baltimoresun.com | url= http://www.baltimoresun.com/sports/ravens/ravens-insider/bal-source-ravens-to-promote-bobby-rainey-to-active-roster-20121016,0,5516939.story | access-date= October 16, 2012 | archive-date= April 14, 2013 | archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20130414220624/http://www.baltimoresun.com/sports/ravens/ravens-insider/bal-source-ravens-to-promote-bobby-rainey-to-active-roster-20121016,0,5516939.story | url-status= dead }}</ref> Rainey never made it on the active game-day roster during the 2012 season. On November 13, he was placed on injured reserve due to a knee injury.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.baltimoreravens.com/news/ravens-roster-moves-18928305|title=Ravens Roster Moves|website=Baltimoreravens.com|access-date=December 6, 2021}}</ref> Rainey earned a Super Bowl ring when the Ravens defeated the [[2012 San Francisco 49ers season|San Francisco 49ers]] in [[Super Bowl XLVII]].

On August 31, 2013, Rainey was released by the Ravens as a part of the team's final roster cuts.

===Cleveland Browns===
On September 1, 2013, Rainey was picked up by the [[Cleveland Browns]] after clearing waivers. He was released by Cleveland after Week 7 of the 2013 season.

===Tampa Bay Buccaneers===
====2013 season====
On October 21, 2013, he was acquired off waivers by the [[Tampa Bay Buccaneers]]. He scored his first career regular season touchdown on November 11. It was the eventual game-winning touchdown in the Buccaneers' 22-19 win over the [[2013 Miami Dolphins season|Miami Dolphins]], serving as Tampa Bay's first win of the 2013 season. On November 17, Rainey had three touchdowns (two rushing and one receiving) and 163 rushing yards in the Buccaneers' win over the [[2013 Atlanta Falcons season|Atlanta Falcons]]. Due to injuries to [[Doug Martin (running back)|Doug Martin]] and [[Mike James (American football)|Mike James]], he would finish his debut Buccaneer season as the team's leading rusher with 137 attempts for 523 yards and five touchdowns. He also had 11 catches for 27 yards and one receiving touchdown.

====2014 season====
On March 5, 2014, Rainey signed a one-year deal to stay with the Buccaneers.<ref>{{cite web|last=Smith|first=Scott|title=Rainey Re-Ups with Bucs|url=http://www.buccaneers.com/news/article-smith/Rainey-Re-Ups-with-Bucs/8c5ddf35-0216-438f-9d01-d69a61c68463|publisher=Buccaneers.com|access-date=March 5, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140306053321/http://www.buccaneers.com/news/article-smith/Rainey-Re-Ups-with-Bucs/8c5ddf35-0216-438f-9d01-d69a61c68463|archive-date=March 6, 2014|url-status=dead}}</ref> Rainey compiled 94 attempts for 406 yards and one touchdown only second to Doug Martin. He also had 33 catches for 315 yards and one receiving touchdown.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Bobby Rainey 2014 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/R/RainBo00/gamelog/2014/ |access-date=2025-05-18 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref>

====2015 season====
On March 10, 2015, the Buccaneers extended a restricted free agent tender offer of $1.542 million for one year to Rainey restricting him from free negotiating with any other and granting Tampa the right to match any offer he receives from other teams. He signed his one-year tender on April 24.<ref>{{cite news|work=NBCSports.com|url=http://profootballtalk.nbcsports.com/2015/04/24/buccaneers-re-sign-rb-bobby-rainey/|title=Buccaneers re-sign RB Bobby Rainey|first=Mike|last=Wilkening|date=April 24, 2015|access-date=January 7, 2016}}</ref>

===New York Giants===
Rainey signed with the [[New York Giants]] on April 11, 2016.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.giants.com/news-and-blogs/article-1/New-York-Giants-sign-RB-Bobby-Rainey-LB-Kelvin-Sheppard-OL-Byron-Stingily/234cd8cd-7905-4c89-8ae7-898fc9739745 |title=New York Giants sign RB Bobby Rainey, LB Kelvin Sheppard, OL Byron Stingily |last=Eisen |first=Michael |date=April 11, 2016 |website=Giants.com |access-date=April 30, 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160426090527/http://www.giants.com/news-and-blogs/article-1/New-York-Giants-sign-RB-Bobby-Rainey-LB-Kelvin-Sheppard-OL-Byron-Stingily/234cd8cd-7905-4c89-8ae7-898fc9739745 |archive-date=April 26, 2016 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

===Baltimore Ravens (second stint)===
On July 26, 2017, Rainey signed with the Baltimore Ravens.<ref>{{cite web|title=Ravens Officially Sign Running Back Bobby Rainey|url=http://www.baltimoreravens.com/news/article-1/Ravens-Officially-Sign-Running-Back-Bobby-Rainey/544302ad-d9e0-4fa7-807d-0310e493e2d7|author=Mink, Ryan|website=BaltimoreRavens.com|date=July 26, 2017}}</ref> On September 1, he was released by the Ravens during final roster cuts.<ref>{{cite web|title=Ravens Announce 24 Roster Moves, Have 13 More To Make|url=http://www.baltimoreravens.com/news/article-1/Ravens-Announce-24-Roster-Moves-Have-13-More-to-Make/914aba64-f454-47d9-932f-e409ccec1735|author=Mink, Ryan|website=BaltimoreRavens.com|date=September 1, 2017|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180118220814/http://www.baltimoreravens.com/news/article-1/Ravens-Announce-24-Roster-Moves-Have-14-More-to-Make/914aba64-f454-47d9-932f-e409ccec1735|archive-date=January 18, 2018}}</ref> Rainey was re-signed on October 10, after an injury to [[Terrance West]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Ravens Re-Sign Running Back Bobby Rainey Following Terrance West's Injury|url=http://www.baltimoreravens.com/news/article-1/Ravens-Re-Sign-Running-Back-Bobby-Rainey-Following-Terrance-Wests-Injury/7bc54edc-b82f-4ebb-aa42-3cc4d5077b02|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180119033633/http://www.baltimoreravens.com/news/article-1/Ravens-Re-Sign-Running-Back-Bobby-Rainey-Following-Terrance-Wests-Injury/7bc54edc-b82f-4ebb-aa42-3cc4d5077b02|url-status=dead|archive-date=January 19, 2018|author=Mink, Ryan|website=BaltimoreRavens.com|date=October 10, 2017}}</ref> In Week 6, against the [[2017 Chicago Bears season|Chicago Bears]], he recorded a 96-yard kickoff return touchdown in the third quarter.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201710150rav.htm |title=Chicago Bears at Baltimore Ravens - October 15th, 2017 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en |access-date=November 7, 2017}}</ref> On November 13, Rainey was released by the Ravens.<ref>{{cite web|title=Ravens Claim Offensive Tackle Andrew Donnal|url=https://www.baltimoreravens.com/news/ravens-claim-offensive-tackle-andrew-donnal-19764318|author=Downing, Garrett|website=BaltimoreRavens.com|date=November 13, 2017}}</ref>

'''Robert Lund Kimball''' (born March 12, 1957) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). Kimball was born on March 12, 1957, in [[Camarillo, California]], where he attended [[Adolfo Camarillo High School|Camarillo High School]].<ref name="PFR">{{cite web | url = https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/K/KimbBo20.htm | title = Bobby Kimball | website = Pro-Football-Reference.com | access-date = March 18, 2024 | archive-date = July 13, 2017 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20170713232717/http://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/K/KimbBo20.htm | url-status = live }}</ref> After high school, he attended [[Ventura College]] for two years, where he played [[college football]]. He then transferred to the [[University of Oklahoma]], where he played [[wide receiver]] for their [[Oklahoma Sooners football|football team]].<ref name="SIGNS">{{Cite news | url = https://www.newspapers.com/article/ventura-county-star-ex-pirate-receiver-s/143613526/ | title = Ex-Pirate receiver signs with Packers | date = June 12, 1979 | access-date = March 18, 2024 | newspaper = [[Ventura County Star]] | type = clipping | via = [[Newspapers.com]] | page = B-1 }}</ref> At the time, Oklahoma was more known for their rushing game, limiting Kimball's opportunities as a pass catcher, although he had a lot of experience blocking.<ref name="LANDS">{{Cite news | url = https://www.newspapers.com/article/ventura-county-star-bobby-kimball-lands/143613569/ | title = Bobby Kimball lands a job with Green Bay | last = Wagner | first = Bill | date = August 30, 1979 | access-date = March 18, 2024 | newspaper = [[Ventura County Star]] | type = clipping | via = [[Newspapers.com]] | page = C-1 }}</ref>

Kimball went undrafted in the [[1979 NFL draft]], although he signed with the [[Green Bay Packers]] as an undrafted free agent. After a solid showing the preseason, he became the only rookie free agent to make the team.<ref name="LANDS"/> He was expected to be utilized primarily on the punt and kick return teams.<ref name="CAREER">{{Cite news | url = https://www.newspapers.com/article/camarillo-star-bobby-kimball-begins-his/143613413/ | title = Bobby Kimball begins his NFL career today | last = Reem | first = Craig | date = September 2, 1979 | access-date = March 18, 2024 | newspaper = [[Camarillo Star]] | type = clipping | via = [[Newspapers.com]] | page = A-11 }}</ref> Part way through his first season, he injured his knee, which required surgery.<ref name="NFLCOLD">{{Cite news | url = https://www.newspapers.com/article/camarillo-star-with-kimball-its-an-nfl/143613480/ | title = With Kimball it's an "NFL cold" | last = Steers | first = Dennis | date = October 29, 1979 | access-date = March 18, 2024 | newspaper = [[Camarillo Star]] | type = clipping | via = [[Newspapers.com]] | page = B-1 }}</ref> He returned the next season, but only played in one game. In total, he played for the Packers for two seasons, appearing in eight games, and recording zero catches.<ref name="PFR"/>

'''Bobby Joseph Wagner''' (born June 27, 1990) is an American professional [[American football|football]] [[linebacker]]. Wagner played [[college football]] for the [[Utah State Aggies football|Utah State Aggies]] and was selected by the [[Seattle Seahawks]] in the second round of the [[2012 NFL draft]]. He spent ten years with the Seahawks before playing for the [[Los Angeles Rams]] in 2022, later returning to Seattle for a second stint in 2023. He then spent two seasons playing for the [[Washington Commanders]].

Regarded as one of the greatest linebackers in NFL history,<ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-12-16 |title=5 Commanders who have to lose reps after inevitable Jayden Daniels bombshell |url=https://riggosrag.com/5-commanders-who-have-lose-reps-after-inevitable-jayden-daniels-bombshell/3 |access-date=2025-12-31 |website=Riggo's Rag |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Pro Football 101: Bobby Wagner ranks No. 88 on the list of best NFL players ever {{!}} Fox Sports |url=https://www.foxsports.com/stories/nfl/pro-football-101-bobby-wagner-ranks-no-88-on-the-list-of-best-nfl-players-ever |access-date=2025-12-31 |website=amp.foxsports.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Adame |first=Tony |date=2025-06-28 |title=Commanders' $118 Million All-Pro LB Called 'Greatest Draft Pick' of Last 25 Years |url=https://heavy.com/sports/nfl/washington-commanders/bobby-wagner-greatest-nfl-draft-picks/ |access-date=2025-12-31 |website=Heavy Sports |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Alfano |first=Jon |date=2025-07-22 |title=Seahawks legend Bobby Wagner ranked among best LBs this century |url=https://www.si.com/nfl/seahawks/onsi/seahawks-news/seattle-seahawks-legend-bobby-wagner-ranked-among-best-linebackers-century |access-date=2025-12-31 |website=Seattle Seahawks On SI |language=en-US}}</ref> Wagner is a member of the [[NFL 2010s All-Decade Team]] and won [[Super Bowl XLVIII]] with the Seahawks in 2013. He is also a ten-time [[Pro Bowl]]er, an eleven-time [[All-Pro]] selection, a three-time NFL combined tackles leader, and leads all active players in career tackles.<ref>{{cite web |title=NFL Tackles Combined Career Leaders (since 1987) |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/leaders/tackles_combined_career.htm |website=Pro Football Reference |access-date=July 27, 2023}}</ref> Wagner won the 2023 [[Art Rooney Award]] and was named the 2025 [[Walter Payton NFL Man of the Year]]. He is also a minority owner of the WNBA's [[Seattle Storm]].

==Early life==
Wagner was born on June 27, 1990, in [[Los Angeles, California]]. He attended [[Colony High School]] in [[Ontario, California]],<ref>{{Cite web |date=2022-07-22 |title=Rams star Bobby Wagner hosts youth football camp at Ontario school where he graduated |url=https://abc7.com/bobby-wagner-rams-colony-high-school-ontario/12066375/ |access-date=2025-04-16 |website=ABC7 Los Angeles |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Klein |first=Gary |date=2022-06-03 |title=SoCal native Bobby Wagner explains why coming home to Rams literally hits home |url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/rams/story/2022-06-02/socal-native-bobby-wagner-feels-at-home-as-a-mnem |access-date=2025-04-16 |website=Los Angeles Times |language=en-US}}</ref> where he played [[high school football]] for the Titans. In 2007, he registered 125 tackles (92 solo, 33 assists), including four sacks as a senior. He also played tight end, tallying 37 catches for 595 yards with 11 touchdowns. He received all-CIF Central Division honors as well as all-Mount Baldy League accolades. He earned second-team California Division 2 all-state honors after helping lead the Titans to a CIF division title and was named to the All-San Bernardino County team. Considered a two-star recruit by ''[[Rivals.com]]'', Wagner's only offer came from [[Utah State Aggies football|Utah State]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Bobby Wagner |url=https://sports.yahoo.com/footballrecruiting/football/recruiting/player-Bobby-Wagner-77948 |url-status=dead |access-date=February 1, 2018 |website=Yahoo! Sports |archive-date=April 26, 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140426221549/https://sports.yahoo.com/footballrecruiting/football/recruiting/player-Bobby-Wagner-77948 }}</ref>

==College career==
Wagner attended [[Utah State University]] from 2008 to 2011.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Bobby Wagner College Stats |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/players/bobby-wagner-1.html |access-date=February 22, 2019 |website=Sports-Reference.com}}</ref> A four-year starter, he recorded 445 tackles, 4.5 [[Quarterback sack|sacks]], and four [[interceptions]] during his career.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Bobby Wagner Career Game Log |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/players/bobby-wagner-1/gamelog/ |access-date=February 22, 2019 |website=Sports-Reference.com}}</ref> As a senior in 2011, Wagner was the [[Western Athletic Conference|WAC]] Defensive Player of the Year after recording 147 tackles, four sacks, and two interceptions.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Denniston |first=Wade |date=July 29, 2011 |title=Wagner tabbed WAC Defensive Player of the Year |url=https://www.hjnews.com/sports/article_5b5f6b1e-b9a2-11e0-b9eb-001cc4c03286.html |access-date=April 7, 2022 |website=HJNews.com}}</ref>

==Professional career==
On January 14, 2012, it was announced that Wagner had accepted his invitation to play in the [[2012 Senior Bowl]]. He became the first Utah State player to play in the game since [[Chris Cooley (American football)|Chris Cooley]] in 2004.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Hoffman |first=Doug |date=January 14, 2012 |title=Utah State football: Linebacker Bobby Wagner picked to play in Senior Bowl |url=https://www.deseret.com/2012/1/14/20391399/utah-state-football-linebacker-bobby-wagner-picked-to-play-in-senior-bowl |access-date=April 7, 2022 |website=Deseret}}</ref> On January 28, 2012, Wagner played in the [[Senior Bowl]] and recorded 22 combined tackles and an interception for the North team coached by [[Leslie Frazier]] that defeated the South team 23–13. He was named the Senior Bowl MVP and was also named the North's Most Outstanding Player.<ref>{{Cite web |date=January 28, 2012 |title=Utah State's Bobby Wagner Named North's Most Outstanding Player Saturday In Senior Bowl |url=https://www.cachevalleydaily.com/news/archive/2012/01/28/d0d27d2a-e6d7-5569-b43e-4b955765faa3/#.Yk9FQCjMLIV |access-date=January 28, 2018 |website=Cache Valley Daily}}</ref> Wagner received an invitation to the [[NFL Scouting Combine]], but was unable to attend after coming down with [[pneumonia]]. On March 30, 2012, Wagner attended Utah State's [[Pro Day]] and impressed scouts and team representatives after performing all of the combine drills. He displayed his versatility and athleticism throughout his workout and helped solidify himself as a top linebacker.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Siddoway |first=Jon |date=March 31, 2012 |title=NFL Draft 2012: Did Bobby Wagner's Pro Day Push Him into the First Round? |url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/1126764-nfl-draft-2012-did-bobby-wagners-pro-day-push-him-into-the-first-round |access-date=April 7, 2022 |website=Bleacher Report}}</ref> His 40-yard dash and broad jump would have finished first among all linebackers in at the NFL combine and his vertical would have tied with [[California Golden Bears football|California's]] [[Mychal Kendricks]] for first. His broad jump was five inches better than any linebacker at the combine and would have finished third among all positions.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Bloom |first=Sigmund |date=March 30, 2012 |title=2012 NFL Draft Sleeper: Utah State LB Bobby Wagner Runs 4.45 at His Pro Day |url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/1126172-2012-nfl-draft-sleeper-utah-state-lb-bobby-wagner-runs-445-at-his-pro-day |access-date=January 28, 2018 |website=Bleacher Report}}</ref> At the conclusion of the pre-draft process, Wagner was projected to be a second round pick by NFL draft experts and scouts. He was ranked the fourth best outside linebacker in the draft by NFLDraftScout.com.<ref name="scout" />

===Seattle Seahawks===
====2012====
{{see also|2012 Seattle Seahawks season}}
The [[Seattle Seahawks]] selected Wagner in the second round (47th overall) of the [[2012 NFL draft]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=2012 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2012/draft.htm |access-date=February 22, 2019 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]]}}</ref> He is the 11th highest player selected in the NFL draft from Utah State and the highest since [[Rulon Jones]] in [[1980 NFL draft|1980]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=The Football Database: Utah State NFL Draft History |url=https://www.footballdb.com/draft/college.html?c=Utah+State |access-date=January 28, 2018 |website=FootballDB}}</ref> The Seahawks also drafted his Utah State teammate [[Robert Turbin]] in the fourth round.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2012 Seattle Seahawks Draftees |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/teams/sea/2012_draft.htm |access-date=February 22, 2019 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]]}}</ref> On May 7, 2012, the Seahawks signed Wagner to a four-year, $4.30 million contract that includes $2.51 million guaranteed and a [[signing bonus]] of $1.57 million.<ref name="spotrac">{{Cite web |title=Bobby Wagner contracts |url=https://www.spotrac.com/nfl/los-angeles-rams/bobby-wagner-9857/ |access-date=April 7, 2022 |website=Spotrac.com}}</ref>

Wagner entered [[training camp (NFL)|training camp]] competing for the vacant starting middle linebacker role against [[Barrett Ruud]] and [[Matt McCoy (American football)|Matt McCoy]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Bloom |first=Sigmund |date=May 15, 2012 |title=Seattle Seahawks: Bobby Wagner Will Compete for Starting LB Position Right Away |url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/1183983-bobby-wagner-will-compete-to-start-at-middle-linebacker-right-away-for-seahawks |access-date=January 28, 2018 |website=bleacherreport.com}}</ref> Although Ruud was initially supposed to replace [[David Hawthorne]], an injury sidelined him during organized team activities, giving Wagner valuable time with the first team defense.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Farnsworth |first=Clara |date=July 30, 2012 |title=Ruud joins the competition |url=http://www.seahawks.com/news/2012/07/30/ruud-joins-competition |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180129195302/http://www.seahawks.com/news/2012/07/30/ruud-joins-competition |archive-date=January 29, 2018 |access-date=January 28, 2018 |website=Seattle Seahawks}}</ref> Head coach [[Pete Carroll]] named Wagner the starting middle linebacker, along with outside linebackers [[K. J. Wright]] and [[Leroy Hill]], to start the regular season.<ref>{{Cite web |date=September 7, 2012 |title=2012 Seattle Seahawks season preview part 4: The defensive depth chart |url=http://nwsportsbeat.com/seahawks/2012-seattle-defense-depth-chart-roster-analysis-7912/ |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180129141208/http://www.nwsportsbeat.com/seahawks/2012-seattle-defense-depth-chart-roster-analysis-7912/ |archive-date=January 29, 2018 |access-date=January 28, 2018 |website=NW Sports Beat}}</ref>

He made his professional regular season debut and first career start in the Seahawks season-opener at the [[Arizona Cardinals]] and recorded four combined tackles during their 20–16 loss.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Seattle Seahawks at Arizona Cardinals – September 9th, 2012 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201209090crd.htm |access-date=November 2, 2022 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> In Week 5, Wagner recorded five combined tackles and made his first career sack on [[Cam Newton]] in the Seahawks' 16–12 victory.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Seattle Seahawks at Carolina Panthers – October 7th, 2012 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201210070car.htm |access-date=November 2, 2022 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> The next week, he made a season-high 14 combined tackles in a 24–23 victory against the [[New England Patriots]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=New England Patriots at Seattle Seahawks – October 14th, 2012 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201210140sea.htm |access-date=November 2, 2022 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> On November 25, 2012, Wagner recorded nine combined tackles, two pass deflections, and intercepted his first career pass off [[Miami Dolphins]] quarterback [[Ryan Tannehill]] during a 24–21 loss.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Seattle Seahawks at Miami Dolphins – November 25th, 2012 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201211250mia.htm |access-date=November 2, 2022 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> On December 9, 2012, he collected eight combined tackles, two pass deflections, and intercepted two passes off of [[John Skelton (American football)|John Skelton]] in a 58–0 |access-date=November 2, 2022 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> Wagner finished his rookie season with 140 combined tackles (87 solo), four pass deflections, three interceptions. and two sacks in 16 games and 15 starts.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Bobby Wagner 2012 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/W/WagnBo00/gamelog/2012/ |access-date=November 2, 2022 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> [[Pro Football Focus]] (PFF) ranked him the second best inside linebacker in 2012 and the best rookie linebacker during the season.<ref>{{Cite web |title=PFF News & Analysis |url=https://www.profootballfocus.com/blog/2013/01/15/2012-pff-all-rookie-team/2 |access-date=February 1, 2018 |website=Pro Football Focus}}</ref> He was named to the PFWA All-Rookie Team.<ref name="2012allrookie">{{Cite web |title=2012 NFL All-Rookie Team |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/awards/nfl-all-rookie-2012.htm |access-date=2024-08-03 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

The Seahawks finished second in the [[NFC West]] with an 11–5 record and received a playoff berth.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2012 Seattle Seahawks Statistics & Players |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/teams/sea/2012.htm |access-date=February 22, 2019 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> On January 6, 2013, Wagner started in his first career playoff game and recorded nine combined tackles during a 24–14 victory at the [[Washington Redskins]] in the [[National Football Conference]] (NFC) [[2012–13 NFL playoffs#NFC: Seattle Seahawks 24, Washington Redskins 14|Wild Card Round]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Wild Card – Seattle Seahawks at Washington Redskins – January 6th, 2013 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201301060was.htm |access-date=February 22, 2019 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]]}}</ref> They were eliminated by the [[Atlanta Falcons]] in the [[2012–13 NFL playoffs#NFC: Atlanta Falcons 30, Seattle Seahawks 28|Divisional Round]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Divisional Round – Seattle Seahawks at Atlanta Falcons – January 13th, 2013 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201301130atl.htm |access-date=February 22, 2019 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]]}}</ref>

====2013: Super Bowl championship====
{{see also|2013 Seattle Seahawks season}}
Wagner remained the starting middle linebacker to start the 2013 regular season under new defensive coordinator [[Dan Quinn (American football)|Dan Quinn]]. On September 22, 2013, he recorded nine combined tackles, deflected a pass, and intercepted [[Chad Henne]] as the Seahawks defeated the [[Jacksonville Jaguars]] and Seattle's former defensive coordinator [[Gus Bradley]] 45–17, who became the Jaguars head coach in 2013.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Jacksonville Jaguars at Seattle Seahawks – September 22nd, 2013 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201309220sea.htm |access-date=November 2, 2022 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> Wagner missed the first two games of his career (Weeks 6–7) after suffering a high ankle sprain.<ref>{{Cite web |date=October 28, 2013 |title=Seahawks LB Hill returns from injury to face Rams |url=https://www.foxsports.com/stories/nfl/seahawks-lb-hill-returns-from-injury-to-face-rams |access-date=April 7, 2022 |website=FOX Sports}}</ref> In Week 9, Wagner collected 11 combined tackles and was credited with 1.5 sacks on [[Mike Glennon]] during a 27–24 win over the [[Tampa Bay Buccaneers]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Tampa Bay Buccaneers at Seattle Seahawks – November 3rd, 2013 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201311030sea.htm |access-date=November 2, 2022 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> On December 29, 2013, he made a season-high 12 combined tackles during a 27–9 victory against the [[St. Louis Rams]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=St. Louis Rams at Seattle Seahawks – December 29th, 2013 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201312290sea.htm |access-date=November 2, 2022 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> He finished the season with 120 combined tackles (72 solo), seven pass deflections, five sacks, and two interceptions in 14 games and 14 starts.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Bobby Wagner 2013 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/W/WagnBo00/gamelog/2013/ |access-date=November 2, 2022 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> PFF ranked Wagner the 61st best player in the league in 2013, regardless of position.<ref>{{cite web | last=Larrabee | first=Kirk | title=Five Seahawks make Pro Football Focus 2014 rankings | website=247Sports | date=2015-05-19 | url=https://247sports.com/article/five-seahawks-make-pro-football-focus-2014-rankings-37351834/ | access-date=2025-07-10}}</ref>

The Seahawks finished the season atop their division with a 13–3 record.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2013 Seattle Seahawks Statistics & Players |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/teams/sea/2013.htm |access-date=February 22, 2019 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]]}}</ref> On January 19, 2014, Wagner started in the [[2013–14 NFL playoffs#NFC Championship Game: Seattle Seahawks 23, San Francisco 49ers 17|NFC Championship]] and recorded 15 combined tackles during a 23–17 victory over the [[San Francisco 49ers]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=NFC Championship – San Francisco 49ers at Seattle Seahawks – January 19th, 2014 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201401190sea.htm |access-date=November 2, 2022 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> On February 2, 2014, Wagner started in his first career Super Bowl and made ten combined tackles as the Seahawks routed the [[Denver Broncos]] 43–8 and won [[Super Bowl XLVIII]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Super Bowl XLVIII – Seattle Seahawks vs. Denver Broncos – on February 2nd, 2014 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201402020den.htm |access-date=November 3, 2017 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]]}}</ref>

====2014====
{{see also|2014 Seattle Seahawks season}}
[[File:Bobby Wagner 2014.jpg|thumb|left|Wagner with the [[Seattle Seahawks]] in 2014]]
Wagner, K. J. Wright, and [[Bruce Irvin (American football)|Bruce Irvin]] returned as the starting linebacker corps in 2014. Wagner started the Seahawks' season-opener against the [[Green Bay Packers]] and recorded a season-high 14 combined tackles during a 36–16 victory on ''[[Thursday Night Football]]''.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Green Bay Packers at Seattle Seahawks – September 4th, 2014 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201409040sea.htm |access-date=November 2, 2022 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> Unfortunately, he missed five games (Weeks 7–11) after suffering [[turf toe]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Farnsworth |first=Clare |date=October 13, 2017 |title=Injuries to Bobby Wagner and Byron Maxwell latest concerns for Seahawks |url=http://www.seahawks.com/news/2014/10/13/injuries-bobby-wagner-and-byron-maxwell-latest-concerns-seahawks |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170818133158/http://www.seahawks.com/news/2014/10/13/injuries-bobby-wagner-and-byron-maxwell-latest-concerns-seahawks |archive-date=August 18, 2017 |access-date=January 29, 2018 |website=Seattle Seahawks}}</ref> On December 14, 2014, Wagner recorded his fourth game with at least ten combined tackles and sacked [[Colin Kaepernick]] during a 17–7 victory over the 49ers. Wagner finished the 2014 season with 104 combined tackles (67 solo), nine tackles for a loss, three pass deflections, and two sacks in 11 games and 11 starts.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Bobby Wagner 2014 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/W/WagnBo00/gamelog/2014/ |access-date=November 2, 2022 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> Even though he missed five  games, he was voted into his first [[Pro Bowl]] and was named First Team [[All-Pro]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Farnsworth |first=Clare |date=January 2, 2015 |title=Bobby Wagner joins Earl Thomas and Richard Sherman as first team All-Pro selections |url=http://www.seahawks.com/news/2015/01/02/bobby-wagner-joins-earl-thomas-and-richard-sherman-first-team-all-pro-selections |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150731104446/http://www.seahawks.com/news/2015/01/02/bobby-wagner-joins-earl-thomas-and-richard-sherman-first-team-all-pro-selections |archive-date=July 31, 2015 |access-date=August 2, 2015 |website=Seattle Seahawks}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=2014 NFL Pro Bowlers |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2014/probowl.htm |access-date=November 2, 2022 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> For the third straight season, the Seahawks' defense finished first in the NFL in points allowed, making Wagner a key starter on the top defense every year of his career so far.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2014 NFL Standings & Team Stats |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2014/index.htm |access-date=February 22, 2019 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]]}}</ref> For his efforts that season, he received a single MVP vote from [[Tony Dungy]], largely due to the Seahawks allowing 20.4 points per game without Wagner and 6.5 points per game in the six games after he returned from an injury.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Bibber |first=Ryan Van |date=February 1, 2015 |title=Dungy defends unusual MVP vote |url=https://www.sbnation.com/nfl/2015/2/1/7959231/tony-dungy-explains-bobby-wagner-mvp-vote-nfl-honors |access-date=February 22, 2019 |website=SBNation.com}}</ref>

On February 1, 2015, the Seahawks played in [[Super Bowl XLIX]] after defeating the Panthers in the [[2014–15 NFL playoffs#NFC: Seattle Seahawks 31, Carolina Panthers 17|Divisional Round]] and then the Packers in the [[2014–15 NFL playoffs#NFC: Seattle Seahawks 28, Green Bay Packers 22 (OT)|NFC Championship]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Divisional Round – Carolina Panthers at Seattle Seahawks – January 10th, 2015 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201501100sea.htm |access-date=November 2, 2022 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=NFC Championship – Green Bay Packers at Seattle Seahawks – January 18th, 2015 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201501180sea.htm |access-date=November 2, 2022 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> Wagner recorded 12 combined tackles, deflected a pass, and intercepted a pass attempt by [[Tom Brady]] in the Seahawks 28–24 last-second loss to the Patriots.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Super Bowl XLIX – Seattle Seahawks vs. New England Patriots – February 1st, 2015 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201502010sea.htm |access-date=November 2, 2022 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> Wagner made the NFL Top 100 Players for the first time in his career after he garnered enough votes from his NFL peers to finish ranked 69th in the ''[[NFL Top 100 Players of 2015]]''.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2015 NFL Top 100 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/awards/2015-nfl-top-100.htm |access-date=November 2, 2022 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

====2015====
{{see also|2015 Seattle Seahawks season}}
On August 2, 2015, the Seahawks signed Wagner to a four-year, $43 million contract extension that included $19.97 million guaranteed and a signing bonus of $8 million.<ref name="spotrac" /><ref>{{Cite web |last=Rosenthal |first=Gregg |date=August 2, 2015 |title=Seahawks, Bobby Wagner agree to $43M extension |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/seahawks-lb-bobby-wagner-signs-43m-extension-0ap3000000505826 |access-date=April 7, 2022 |website=NFL.com}}</ref>

Irvin, Wright, and Wagner remained the starters under new defensive coordinator [[Kris Richard]] to begin 2015. On October 11, 2015, Wagner recorded seven combined tackles, a pass deflection and a fumble recovery, and scored his first career touchdown during a 27–24 [[overtime (American football)|overtime]] loss to the [[Cincinnati Bengals]]. Defensive end [[Michael Bennett (defensive lineman, born 1985)|Michael Bennett]] caused Bengals' running back [[Rex Burkhead]] to fumble in the third quarter, which Wagner recovered and returned it 23 yards for a touchdown.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Seattle Seahawks at Cincinnati Bengals – October 11th, 2015 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201510110cin.htm |access-date=November 2, 2022 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> Wagner missed the Seahawks' Week 6 loss to the Carolina Panthers with a pectoral strain.<ref>{{Cite web |date=October 12, 2015 |title=Report: Seahawks LB Bobby Wagner (pectoral strain) out indefinitely |url=https://www.si.com/nfl/2015/10/12/seattle-seahawks-bobby-wagner-pectoral-strain-injury-out |access-date=January 29, 2018 |website=Sports Illustrated}}</ref> In Week 10, Wagner collected 11 combined tackles, deflected a pass, recovered a fumble, and scored his second touchdown of the season, as the Seahawks lost to the [[Arizona Cardinals]], 39–32. In the fourth quarter of that game, linebacker [[K. J. Wright]] sacked quarterback [[Carson Palmer]] for a nine-yard loss and jarred the ball loose resulting in a fumble. Wagner recovered the fumble and returned it for a 22-yard touchdown.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Arizona Cardinals at Seattle Seahawks – November 15th, 2015 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201511150sea.htm |access-date=November 2, 2022 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> On November 29, 2015, he tied his season-high of 12 combined tackles and deflected a pass in Seattle's 39–30 victory over the [[Pittsburgh Steelers]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Pittsburgh Steelers at Seattle Seahawks – November 29th, 2015 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201511290sea.htm |access-date=November 2, 2022 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

He finished the 2015 season with 114 combined tackles (67 solo) and seven pass deflections, and was credited with only half a sack in 15 games and 15 starts. This marked his first and only season without a solo sack.<ref name="Stats2015">{{Cite web |title=Bobby Wagner 2015 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/W/WagnBo00/gamelog/2015/ |access-date=November 2, 2022 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> Wagner finished second on the team in tackles, falling two behind leader K. J. Wright.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2015 Seattle Seahawks Rosters, Stats, Schedule, Team Draftees, Injury Reports |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/teams/sea/2015.htm |access-date=November 2, 2022 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> He was voted to the [[2016 Pro Bowl]] and was named to the [[Associated Press]] All-Pro second team.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2015 NFL Pro Bowlers |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2015/probowl.htm |access-date=November 2, 2022 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> PFF ranked Wagner the 30th-best linebacker in 2015. His teammate K. J. Wright was ranked the sixth-best linebacker by PFF and [[Bruce Irvin (American football)|Bruce Irvin]] was ranked 15th.{{citation needed|date=September 2024}}

The Seahawks finished second in the NFC West with a 10–6 record.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2015 NFL Standings & Team Stats |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2015/index.htm |access-date=February 22, 2019 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]]}}</ref> They went on to defeat the Vikings, 10–9, in the NFC [[2015–16 NFL playoffs#NFC: Seattle Seahawks 10, Minnesota Vikings 9|Wild Card Round]] and then lost, 31–24, to the Panthers in the [[2015–16 NFL playoffs#NFC: Carolina Panthers 31, Seattle Seahawks 24|Divisional Round]] as Wagner recorded 13 combined tackles.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Wild Card – Seattle Seahawks at Minnesota Vikings – January 10th, 2016 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201601100min.htm |access-date=February 22, 2019 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]]}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Divisional Round – Seattle Seahawks at Carolina Panthers – January 17th, 2016 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201601170car.htm |access-date=February 22, 2019 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]]}}</ref> On January 31, 2016, Wagner played in his first Pro Bowl game and recorded ten combined tackles to help [[Michael Irvin|Team Irvin]] defeat [[Jerry Rice|Team Rice]], 49–27, and win the 2016 Pro Bowl.<ref name="Stats2015" />

====2017====
{{see also|2017 Seattle Seahawks season}}

====2018====
{{see also|2018 Seattle Seahawks season}}
On December 2, Wagner logged 12 combined tackles, one sack, two tackles for loss, and two takeaways near the goal line in a 43–16 home win over the 49ers. For his first takeaway, in the second quarter, he forced a fumble from [[Jeffery Wilson]] at the Seahawk 5-yard line, recovered it at the 3, and returned it 11 yards to the 14. Later, in the fourth quarter, he intercepted a pass from [[Nick Mullens]] at the 2-yard line and ran it back 98 yards for a touchdown, his first career pick six, to set the Seahawk franchise record for longest play.<ref>{{Cite web |title=San Francisco 49ers at Seattle Seahawks – December 2nd, 2018 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201812020sea.htm |access-date=February 22, 2019 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]]}}</ref> He earned NFC Defensive Player of the Week honors for his game against San Francisco.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2018 NFL Week 13 Leaders & Scores |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2018/week_13.htm |access-date=November 1, 2022 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> On December 10, against the [[2018 Minnesota Vikings season|Minnesota Vikings]], Wagner was a part of many key third and fourth down stops as well as blocking a field goal by kicker [[Dan Bailey (American football)|Dan Bailey]]. The block proved to be controversial with the NFL eventually saying he should have been called for a penalty after using his teammates for leverage.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Minnesota Vikings at Seattle Seahawks – December 10th, 2018 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201812100sea.htm |access-date=February 22, 2019 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]]}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web sack, 138 total tackles (84 solo), one interception, 11 passes defended, and two forced fumbles.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Bobby Wagner 2018 Game Log
