===Los Angeles Rams===
Wagner signed a five-year contract worth up to $65 million with the [[Los Angeles Rams]] on March 31, 2022.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Gordon |first=Grant |date=March 31, 2022 |title=Rams signing LB Bobby Wagner to five-year, $50M deal |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/bobby-wagner-rams-sign-lb-five-year-50m-deal-seahawks |access-date=March 31, 2022 |website=NFL.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Baer |first=Jack |date=March 31, 2022 |title=Ex Seahawks LB Bobby Wagner signs with the Rival Rams for a 5 Year $50 Million Deal |url=https://sports.yahoo.com/ex-seahawks-lb-bobby-wagner-rams-5-year-50-million-deal-192024692.html |access-date=November 1, 2022 |website=Yahoo! Sports}}</ref> Playing and starting in all 17 games for the Rams, Wagner recorded six sacks, 140 total tackles, two interceptions, and five passes defended as L.A. fell to a 5-12 record the year after winning [[Super Bowl LVI]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Bobby Wagner 2022 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/W/WagnBo00/gamelog/2022/ |access-date=February 29, 2024 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> Following the 2022 season, Wagner was named second-team All-Pro for a second year in a row.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2022 NFL All-Pros |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2022/allpro.htm |access-date=September 7, 2023 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> He was ranked 62nd by his fellow players on the [[NFL Top 100 Players of 2023]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=2023 NFL Top 100 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/awards/2023-nfl-top-100.htm |access-date=September 7, 2023 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> The Rams released Wagner for salary cap reasons on February 23, 2023.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Wagoner |first=Nick |date=February 23, 2023 |title=Sources: All-Pro LB Wagner, Rams to part ways |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/35720839/sources-all-pro-lb-bobby-wagner-rams-agree-part-ways |access-date=February 26, 2023 |website=ESPN.com |language=en}}</ref>

===Seattle Seahawks (second stint)===
Wagner signed a one-year contract worth up to $7 million to return to the Seahawks on March 25, 2023.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Boyle|first=John |date=March 25, 2023 |title=Welcome Back, Bobby Wagner|url=https://www.seahawks.com/news/seahawks-agree-to-terms-with-bobby-wagner|access-date=March 25, 2023|website=Seahawks.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Condotta |first=Bob |date=March 25, 2023 |title=Seahawks are reportedly bringing back Bobby Wagner|url=https://www.seattletimes.com/sports/seahawks/seahawks-are-reportedly-bringing-back-lb-bobby-wagner/|access-date=March 25, 2023 |website=Seattle Times}}</ref> He led the league in total tackles with 183 in the 2023 season.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2023 NFL Defense |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2023/defense.htm |access-date=February 29, 2024 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> He was named as a Pro Bowler for the ninth time.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2023 NFL Pro Bowlers |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2023/probowl.htm |access-date=February 29, 2024 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> In addition, he had 3.5 sacks, three passes defended, and one fumble recovery in 17 games and 16 starts.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Bobby Wagner 2023 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/W/WagnBo00/gamelog/2023/ |access-date=February 29, 2024 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> He was a second team All-Pro named by the Associated Press.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2023 NFL All-Pros |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2023/allpro.htm |access-date=February 29, 2024 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> He won the [[Art Rooney Award]] in 2023.<ref>{{Cite web |date=February 8, 2024 |title=List of 'NFL Honors' award winners from 2023 NFL season |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/list-of-nfl-honors-award-winners-from-2023-nfl-season |access-date=February 9, 2024 |website=NFL.com |language=en-US}}</ref>

===Washington Commanders===

On March 15, 2024, Wagner signed a one-year, $8.5 million contract with the [[Washington Commanders]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nfl.com/news/commanders-signing-bobby-wagner-to-one-year-deal|title=Commanders signing LB Bobby Wagner to one-year deal|date=March 13, 2024|accessdate=March 15, 2024|first=Nick|last=Shook|work=NFL.com}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.commanders.com/news/commanders-sign-lb-bobby-wagner|title=Commanders sign LB Bobby Wagner|work=Commanders.com|date=March 15, 2024|accessdate=March 15, 2024}}</ref> In Week 4 against the [[Arizona Cardinals]], he surpassed [[Zach Thomas]] for fourth [[List of NFL career tackles leaders|most career tackles]] in NFL history.<ref>{{cite web |title=Commanders-Cardinals Stats & Snaps |url=https://www.commanders.com/news/commanders-cardinals-stats-snaps-x3883 |website=Commanders.com |access-date=September 30, 2024 |date=September 30, 2024|quote=Wagner (1,734) has passed LB Zach Thomas (1,733) for the fourth-most tackles in NFL history.}}</ref> Wagner recorded at least 100 tackles in a season for the 13th consecutive year, trailing [[London Fletcher]] for the second-longest streak in NFL history.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Salvatore |first1=Hayley |title=Bobby Wagner's message to 'have fun' on field resonated with teammates |url=https://www.commanders.com/news/bobby-wagner-s-message-to-have-fun-on-field-resonated-with-teammates |website=Commanders.com |access-date=December 5, 2024 |date=December 4, 2024 |quote=The 34-year-old recorded his 100th tackle of the season in the first quarter of the matchup, marking his 13th-straight season with at least 100 stops. The feat puts Wagner in the same category as former Washington linebacker London Fletcher, the only other player in NFL history with the same career tackles record.}}</ref> He earned second-team [[2024 All-Pro Team|All-Pro honors]] after recording 132 tackles, which led the team, as well as two sacks, four pass breakups, a forced fumble, and two fumble recoveries.<ref>{{cite web |author1=Washington Commanders Public Relations |title=McLaurin, Wagner, Luvu, Ekeler named Second Team All-Pro by Associated Press |url=https://www.commanders.com/news/mclaurin-wagner-luvu-ekeler-named-second-team-all-pro-by-associated-press |website=Commanders.com |access-date=January 10, 2025 |date=January 10, 2025}}</ref> Wagner also was named the team's nominee for the [[Walter Payton NFL Man of the Year Award]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Bobby Wagner nominated for 2024 Walter Payton Man of the Year award |url=https://www.commanders.com/news/bobby-wagner-nominated-for-2024-walter-payton-man-of-the-year-award |website=Commanders.com |access-date=December 6, 2024 |date=December 5, 2024}}</ref> He was ranked 74th by his fellow players on the [[NFL Top 100 Players of 2025]].<ref>{{Cite web| last=Selby | first=Zach | date=July 17, 2025 | title= Bobby Wagner ranked No. 74 on NFL's Top 100 list | work=Commanders.com | url= https://www.commanders.com/news/bobby-wagner-ranked-no-74-on-nfl-s-top-100-list | access-date=June 21, 2026}}</ref>

On March 6, 2025, Wagner signed a one-year contract extension worth $9.5 million.<ref name="x578">{{Cite web |last=Williams |first=Charean |author-link=Charean Williams |date=2025-03-06 |title=Commanders re-sign LB Bobby Wagner |url=https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/profootballtalk/rumor-mill/news/commanders-re-sign-lb-bobby-wagner |access-date=2025-03-07 |website=NBC Sports}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.commanders.com/news/commanders-re-sign-lb-bobby-wagner|work=Commanders.com|title=Commanders re-sign LB Bobby Wagner|date=March 7, 2025|accessdate=March 7, 2025}}</ref> On January 4, 2026, during Washington's final regular season game, Wagner recorded five combined tackles to reach 2,000 combined tackles in his career, becoming the third player in NFL history to reach the mark after [[Ray Lewis]] and [[London Fletcher]].<ref>{{cite web |last=Selby |first=Zach |date=January 7, 2026 |title='Sustained dominance': London Fletcher praises Bobby Wagner for joining 2K tackle club |url=https://www.commanders.com/news/london-fletcher-bobby-wagner-2000-tackles |access-date=January 7, 2026 |website=Commanders.com}}</ref> He finished the season with 162 tackles, 4.5 sacks, four pass breakups, and two interceptions.<ref>{{Cite web| title=Bobby Wagner 2025 Game Log | work=Pro Football Reference | url= https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/W/WagnBo00/gamelog/2025/ | access-date=June 21, 2026}}</ref> He won the 2025 NFL Walter Peyton Man of the Year.<ref>{{Cite web| last=Gordon | first=Grant | date=February 5, 2026 | title= Commanders LB Bobby Wagner named 2025 Walter Payton NFL Man of the Year | work=NFL.com | url= https://www.nfl.com/news/commanders-lb-bobby-wagner-named-2025-walter-payton-nfl-man-of-the-year | access-date=June 21, 2026}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Wagner had a close relationship with his mother, Phenia, who passed away after complications from a [[stroke]] in 2009, Wagner's freshman year of college.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2016-01-08 |title=Seahawks linebacker Bobby Wagner never forgets his mother, his greatest loss |url=https://www.seattletimes.com/sports/seahawks/seahawks-linebacker-bobby-wagner-never-forgets-his-greatest-loss/ |access-date=2026-02-10 |website=The Seattle Times |language=en-US}}</ref> Wagner started the FAST54 Phenia Mae Fund in her honor, partnering with hospitals to help stroke patients and promote stroke education.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Commanders LB Bobby Wagner named 2025 Walter Payton NFL Man of the Year |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/commanders-lb-bobby-wagner-named-2025-walter-payton-nfl-man-of-the-year |access-date=2026-02-10 |website=NFL.com |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=FAST54 {{!}} Phenia Mae Fund |url=https://www.fastfivefour.com/ |access-date=2026-02-10 |website=FAST54 {{!}} Phenia Mae Fund |language=en-US}}</ref>

In January 2024, Wagner began an 18-month online course from [[Howard University]] to earn a [[Master of Business Administration]] (MBA) degree.<ref>{{Cite web |date=March 15, 2024 |title=Commanders LB Bobby Wagner lured to Washington in part by MBA pursuit |url=https://www.foxsports.com/stories/nfl/commanders-lb-bobby-wagner-lured-to-washington-in-part-by-mba-pursuit |access-date=11 December 2024 |website=Fox Sports}}</ref> In July 2025, he became a minority owner of the [[Women's National Basketball Association]] (WNBA) team [[Seattle Storm]].<ref name="Wagner">{{cite web |title=Bobby Wagner Joins Seattle Storm Ownership Group |url=https://storm.wnba.com/news/bobby-wagner |website=storm.wnba.com |access-date=July 23, 2025 |date=July 23, 2025}}</ref>

In August 2024, Wagner purchased and opened a franchise location of the [[Crumbl Cookies]] bakery chain at The Landing shopping mall in Renton, Washington. Wagner stated that opening the Crumbl location was "one of the steps I'm looking to take to stay connected to the beautiful city of Seattle."<ref>{{cite web |date=September 6, 2024 |title=Bobby Wagner Is Opening a Crumbl Cookie Shop in Renton |url=https://seattle.eater.com/2024/9/6/24237667/bobby-wagner-opening-crumbl-cookies-renton |access-date=January 21, 2026 |website=Eater Seattle}}</ref>

'''Bobby Bryndale Massie''' (born August 1, 1989) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was an [[offensive tackle]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Ole Miss Rebels football|Ole Miss Rebels]]. He was selected by the [[Arizona Cardinals]] in the fourth round of the [[2012 NFL draft]]. He also played for the [[Chicago Bears]] and [[Denver Broncos]].

==College career==
Massie played three seasons for Ole Miss becoming a full-time starter midway through his [[freshman]] year. He started all 12 games at right tackle in both 2010 and 2011—his [[Sophomore year|sophomore]] and [[Junior (education year)|junior]] years. He wore number 79.

Massie announced on January 6, 2012, that he would forgo his senior year and enter the [[2012 NFL draft]].<ref>[http://www.clarionledger.com/article/20120107/SPORTS030103/201070341/Rebels-OT-Massie-opts-NFL-draft Rebels OT Massie opts for NFL draft]</ref>

===Arizona Cardinals===
Massie was considered one of the best fifteen offensive tackle prospects for the [[2012 NFL draft]] by NFLDraftScout.com.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.nfldraftscout.com/ratings/profilexnews.php?pyid=89450&draftyear=2012&genpos=OT |title=NFL Draft Scout |access-date=February 7, 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120604023740/http://www.nfldraftscout.com/ratings/profilexnews.php?pyid=89450&draftyear=2012&genpos=OT |archive-date=June 4, 2012 |url-status=dead }}</ref> On April 28, 2012, Massie was selected by the [[Arizona Cardinals]] in the fourth round (112th pick overall) of the NFL Draft.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2012 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2012/draft.htm |access-date=2023-05-14 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> On September 5, 2015, Massie was suspended for the first two games of the 2015 season for violating the NFL's Policy and Program on Substances of Abuse.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/cardinals-bobby-massie-suspended-for-two-games-0ap3000000508673 |title=Cardinals' Bobby Massie suspended for two games |last=Wesseling |first=Chris |date=September 5, 2015 |website=NFL.com |access-date=September 11, 2015}}</ref>

===Chicago Bears===
On March 9, 2016, Massie signed a three-year contract with the [[Chicago Bears]] worth $18 million.<ref>{{cite web|title=Bears agree to terms with OT Massie|url=http://www.chicagobears.com/news/article-1/Bears-agree-to-terms-with-OT-Massie/1ef0992b-a9aa-4e30-98f7-b5fefb74fc8f|author=Mayer, Larry|website=ChicagoBears.com|date=March 9, 2016|access-date=March 9, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160310091032/http://www.chicagobears.com/news/article-1/Bears-agree-to-terms-with-OT-Massie/1ef0992b-a9aa-4e30-98f7-b5fefb74fc8f|archive-date=March 10, 2016|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.spotrac.com/nfl/chicago-bears/bobby-massie/|title=Bobby Massie|last=Spotrac.com|website=Spotrac.com|access-date=March 10, 2016}}</ref>

On January 26, 2019, Massie signed a four-year contract extension with the Bears through the 2022 season.<ref>{{cite web|title=OT Bobby Massie, Bears agree on four-year deal|url=http://www.nfl.com/news/story/0ap3000001013524/article/ot-bobby-massie-bears-agree-on-fouryear-deal|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190127094047/http://www.nfl.com/news/story/0ap3000001013524/article/ot-bobby-massie-bears-agree-on-fouryear-deal|url-status=dead|archive-date=January 27, 2019|author=Gordon, Grant|website=NFL.com|date=January 26, 2019}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Roster Moves: Bears ink Massie to four-year extension|url=https://www.chicagobears.com/news/roster-moves-bears-ink-massie-to-four-year-extension|author=Mayer, Larry|website=ChicagoBears.com|date=January 26, 2019}}</ref>

In Week 2 of the 2020 season against the [[2020 New York Giants season|New York Giants]], Massie recorded his first career catch, a four yard pass intended for tight end [[Jimmy Graham]], during the 17–13 win.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/recap?gameId=401220281 |title=Trubisky 2 TD passes, Barkley hurt as Bears edge Giants |date=September 20, 2020|agency=Associated Press |publisher=ESPN |access-date=September 20, 2020}}</ref> He was placed on injured reserve on November 3, 2020, with a knee injury.<ref>{{cite web|title=Roster Moves: Bears put Massie on IR; Ifedi, Spriggs on COVID-19 list|url=https://www.chicagobears.com/news/roster-moves-bears-put-massie-on-ir-ifedi-spriggs-on-covid-19-list|author=Mayer, Larry|website=ChicagoBears.com|date=November 3, 2020}}</ref> He was designated to return from injured reserve on December 30, and began practicing with the team again,<ref>{{cite news |author=Barbieri, Alyssa |title=Bears designated RT Bobby Massie to return from injured reserve |url=https://bearswire.usatoday.com/2020/12/31/chicago-bears-right-tackle-bobby-massie-returning-injured-reserve/ |website=USAToday.com |date=December 31, 2020 |access-date=February 18, 2021}}</ref> but the team did not activate him before the end of the season.

On March 17, 2021, the Bears declined the option on Massie's contract, making him an unrestricted free agent.<ref>{{cite web | last=Sugrue | first=Brendan | title=Report: Bears will cut ties with RT Bobby Massie | website=Bears Wire |publisher=USA Today| date=2021-03-08 | url=https://bearswire.usatoday.com/story/sports/nfl/bears/2021/03/08/chicago-bears-bobby-massie-release/75981009007/ | access-date=2025-09-01}}</ref>

===Denver Broncos===
On May 12, 2021, Massie signed a one-year contract with the [[Denver Broncos]] worth $4 million.<ref>{{cite news |author=DiLalla, Aric |title=Broncos sign T Bobby Massie to one-year contract |url=https://www.denverbroncos.com/news/broncos-sign-t-bobby-massie-to-one-year-contract |website=DenverBroncos.com |date=May 12, 2021 |access-date=May 13, 2021 |archive-date=November 25, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211125114639/https://www.denverbroncos.com/news/broncos-sign-t-bobby-massie-to-one-year-contract |url-status=dead }}</ref>

'''Boseko Lokombo''' (born October 15, 1990) is a [[Democratic Republic of the Congo|Congolese]]-[[Canadians|Canadian]] former professional [[Canadian football]] [[linebacker]]. During his career from 2014 to 2024, Lokombo played nine seasons in the [[Canadian Football League]] (CFL), eight of them with the [[BC Lions]]. He played [[college football]] at [[Oregon Ducks football|Oregon]]. Lokombo has also been a member of the [[Montreal Alouettes]] and [[Toronto Argonauts]] of the CFL, and the [[Baltimore Ravens]], [[Oakland Raiders]] and [[San Francisco 49ers]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL).

==Early life==
Lokombo was born in [[Kinshasa]], [[Zaire]], but moved to [[Montreal]], [[Quebec]] in 1996. Lokombo was raised in [[Abbotsford, British Columbia]], where he attended [[W. J. Mouat Secondary School]]. As a senior,  he recorded 47 tackles with four interceptions and also played wide receiver and running back. He ran for 1,556 yards on 107 carries (14.54 avg.) and 22 touchdowns, and caught 37 passes for 728 yards. He was named the Provincial AAA Eastern Conference All-Star Offensive MVP. He played his junior prep season at [[South Eugene High School]] in [[Eugene, Oregon]] where he recorded more than 50 tackles.

Considered a three-star recruit by ''[[Rivals.com]]'', he was rated as the 27th best [[outside linebacker]] prospect of his class.<ref>[https://sports.yahoo.com/ncaa/football/recruiting/player-Boseko-Lokombo-82957 Boseko Lokombo – Yahoo Sports]</ref>

==Professional career==
===BC Lions (first stint)===
In the [[Canadian Football League]]'s Amateur Scouting Bureau final rankings, he was ranked as the best player for players eligible in the [[2013 CFL draft]].<ref name="April">{{Cite web |url=https://www.cfl.ca/article/cfl-scouting-bureau-releases-april-rankings |title=CFL Scouting Bureau releases April rankings |access-date=2017-08-24 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150923221839/http://www.cfl.ca/article/cfl-scouting-bureau-releases-april-rankings |archive-date=2015-09-23 |url-status=dead }}</ref> Because he was a probable [[National Football League]] draft selection in [[2014 NFL Draft|2014]], his CFL draft stock fell, leading him to be drafted in the third round, 21st overall, by his hometown [[BC Lions]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Beamish |first=Mike |date=May 4, 2013 |title=Abbotsford's Bo Lokombo has the NFL in his sights despite CFL Draft interest |url=https://vancouversun.com/sports/lions%20-%20football/abbotsfords-bo-lokombo-has-the-nfl-in-his-sights-despite-cfl-draft-interest |access-date=2024-03-18 |website=Vancouver Sun}}</ref> He returned to play with the Oregon Ducks for the [[2013 Oregon Ducks football team|2013 season]], but went undrafted and unsigned in the NFL. He signed with the BC Lions on September 8, 2014. Joining the Lions midway through the season, Lokombo spent one game on the injured list before being activated to the Lions' 46-man roster and appearing in the final seven regular season games as well as the post-season. Seeing action exclusively on special teams, he recorded nine tackles on the year, which was seventh place on the club.

In 2015, Lokombo saw action mostly on special teams. He recorded 26 defensive tackles (12th on the team), despite limited action. He got his first CFL sack on a missed snap in a game at Hamilton. Bo Lokombo led the league on special teams with 24 tackles, earning his first CFL West All-star.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.bclions.com/article/bc-signs-2013-draft-pick |title=Lions sign 2013 draft pick |access-date=2014-09-08 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140914064631/http://www.bclions.com/article/bc-signs-2013-draft-pick |archive-date=2014-09-14 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

The Lions granted early free agent status to Lokombo so he could pursue an NFL opportunity.<ref>{{cite web|title=Lions Grant Lokombo Early Release|url=https://www.cfl.ca/2017/01/30/lions-grant-lokombo-early-release/|date=January 30, 2017|website=CFL.ca}}</ref>

===Baltimore Ravens===
On January 31, 2017, Lokombo signed a reserve/future contract with the [[Baltimore Ravens]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Ravens Sign Two Canadian Football League Players|url=http://www.baltimoreravens.com/news/article-1/Ravens-Sign-Two-Canadian-Football-League-Players/4e8448c7-ddf2-40bc-8b8f-3c12fc37694e|author=Mink, Ryan|website=BaltimoreRavens.com|date=January 31, 2017}}</ref> He was waived on September 2 and was signed to the Ravens' practice squad the next day.<ref>{{cite web|title=Ravens Make 15 Moves To Set 53-Man Roster Ahead Of 2017 Season|url=http://www.baltimoreravens.com/news/article-1/Ravens-Make-15-Moves-To-Set-53-Man-Roster-Ahead-of-2017-Season/bdeb00bc-4c08-4b47-a63d-d0e432ee878a|author=Downing, Garrett|website=BaltimoreRavens.com|date=September 2, 2017|url-status=dead|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20180119035032/http://www.baltimoreravens.com/news/article-1/Ravens-Make-15-Moves-To-Set-53-Man-Roster-Ahead-of-2017-Season/bdeb00bc-4c08-4b47-a63d-d0e432ee878a|archivedate=January 19, 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Ravens Sign Six Players To 2017 Practice Squad|url=http://www.baltimoreravens.com/news/article-1/Ravens-Sign-Six-Players-to-2017-Practice-Squad/e9cfcc18-2439-4b4e-9301-36f8b6183bd0|author=Downing, Garrett|website=BaltimoreRavens.com|date=September 3, 2017|url-status=dead|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20180119001132/http://www.baltimoreravens.com/news/article-1/Ravens-Sign-Six-Players-to-2017-Practice-Squad/e9cfcc18-2439-4b4e-9301-36f8b6183bd0|archivedate=January 19, 2018}}</ref> He was released on September 26.

===Oakland Raiders===
On September 28, 2017, Lokombo was signed to the [[Oakland Raiders]]' practice squad.<ref>{{cite web|title=Raiders Announce Transactions – September 28|url=http://www.raiders.com/news/article-1/Raiders-Announce-Transactions---September-28/796f8afc-bdc8-41ed-8770-65421142a076|website=Raiders.com|date=September 28, 2017|access-date=September 28, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170928230749/http://www.raiders.com/news/article-1/Raiders-Announce-Transactions---September-28/796f8afc-bdc8-41ed-8770-65421142a076|archive-date=September 28, 2017|url-status=dead}}</ref> He was released on October 10.<ref>{{cite web|title=Raiders Sign CB Demetrius McCray|url=http://www.raiders.com/news/article-1/Raiders-Sign-CB-Demetrius-McCray/9a0eb20c-b848-477a-bd95-50024157ffde|website=Raiders.com|date=October 10, 2017}}</ref>

===San Francisco 49ers===
On November 29, 2017, Lokombo was signed to the [[San Francisco 49ers]]' practice squad.<ref>{{cite web|title=49ers Announce Several Roster Moves|url=http://www.49ers.com/news/article-2/49ers-Announce-Several-Roster-Moves/7ba0b9f7-cc44-4c7d-ab37-1b757ce2c218|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180316124603/http://www.49ers.com/news/article-2/49ers-Announce-Several-Roster-Moves/7ba0b9f7-cc44-4c7d-ab37-1b757ce2c218|url-status=dead|archive-date=March 16, 2018|website=49ers.com|date=November 29, 2017}}</ref> He signed a reserve/future contract with the 49ers on January 2, 2018.<ref>{{cite web|title=49ers Sign Nine Players to Reserves/Future Contracts|url=http://www.49ers.com/news/article-2/49ers-Sign-Nine-Players-to-ReservesFuture-Contracts/12a6b325-f167-41b9-9982-b89c872c244b|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180316120732/http://www.49ers.com/news/article-2/49ers-Sign-Nine-Players-to-ReservesFuture-Contracts/12a6b325-f167-41b9-9982-b89c872c244b|url-status=dead|archive-date=March 16, 2018|website=49ers.com|date=January 2, 2018}}</ref> Lokombo was released on April 30.<ref>{{cite web|title=49ers release LB Donavin Newsom, four others to reach roster limit|url=https://www.sacbee.com/sports/nfl/san-francisco-49ers/article210161439.html|website=Sacbee.com|date=April 30, 2018}}</ref>

===BC Lions (second stint)===
On May 7, 2018, the Lions announced that Lokombo would be returning to the CFL, having signed a new contract to play for the Lions.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.tsn.ca/lokombo-returns-to-cfl-signs-with-lions-1.1078796|title=Lokombo returns to CFL, signs with Lions – Article – TSN|date=2018-05-07|work=TSN|access-date=2018-05-08}}</ref> He recorded 71 defensive tackles, 16 special teams tackles, four sacks, and two interceptions in 18 regular season games.<ref name="Alouettes signing">{{cite web|title=Alouettes add Posey, Lokombo and Levels|url=https://en.montrealalouettes.com/2019/02/12/alouettes-add-posey-lokombo-levels/|website=montrealalouettes.com|date=February 12, 2019}}</ref>

=== Montreal Alouettes ===
On the first day of free agency in 2019, Lokombo signed a one-year contract with the [[Montreal Alouettes]].<ref name="Alouettes signing"/> He played in 15 regular season games where he had 51 defensive tackles, 8 special teams tackles, and two interceptions as he split time between [[linebacker]] and [[Safety (gridiron football position)|safety]].

=== Toronto Argonauts ===
Lokombo was traded to the [[Toronto Argonauts]] on January 31, 2020.<ref name="Argonauts trade">{{cite web|title=Trade: Argos acquire Canadian LB Bo Lokombo|url=https://www.argonauts.ca/2020/01/31/trade-argos-acquire-playing-rights-canadian-lb-bo-lokombo/|website=argonauts.ca|date=January 31, 2020}}</ref> He did not play in 2020 due to the cancellation of the [[2020 CFL season]] and was released by the Argonauts on January 31, 2021.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.argonauts.ca/2021/01/31/argos-ink-speller-deal-make-moves/|title=Argos ink Speller to a deal + make other moves|date=January 31, 2021|publisher=[[Toronto Argonauts]]|language=en|access-date=January 31, 2021}}</ref>

===BC Lions (third stint)===
On the day following his Toronto release, Lokombo returned to the Lions on February 1, 2021.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bclions.com/2021/02/01/lions-bring-back-lokombo-sign-guzylak-messam-extension/ |title=Lions Bring Back Lokombo, Sign Guzylak-Messam To Extension |publisher=[[BC Lions]] |date=February 1, 2021}}</ref> He scored his first career touchdown on a 20-yard interception return on September 11 against the [[Ottawa Redblacks]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.cfl.ca/games/6157/ottawa-redblacks-vs-bc-lions/ |title=Ottawa Redblacks vs BC Lions |publisher=[[Canadian Football League]] |date=September 11, 2021}}</ref> Lokombo played in all 14 regular season games and finished with 66 defensive tackles, 11 special teams tackles, four sacks, three interceptions, one forced fumble, and one touchdown. For his strong season, he was named the [[CFL's Most Outstanding Canadian Award|CFL's Most Outstanding Canadian]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.cfl.ca/2021/12/10/recap-bombers-names-laced-cfl-awards/ |title=Recap: Bombers names laced through CFL Awards |publisher=[[Canadian Football League]] |date=December 13, 2021}}</ref>

On January 21, 2025, Lokombo announced his retirement from professional football.<ref>{{cite web |title=Bo Lokombo Retires After Ten Professional Seasons |url=https://www.bclions.com/2025/01/21/bo-lokombo-retires-after-ten-professional-seasons/ |publisher=[[BC Lions]] |date=January 21, 2025}}</ref>

'''Bobby Thompson''' (born January 16, 1947) is an American [[Gridiron football|football]] executive and former [[running back]]. An alumnus of the [[University of Oklahoma]], Thompson played two seasons in the [[National Football League]] (NFL) for the [[Detroit Lions]]<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.nfl.com/player/bobbythompson/2527311/profile |title=Bobby Thompson, RB at NFL.com |website=[[NFL.com]] |access-date=2013-06-14 |archive-date=2014-06-07 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140607010631/http://www.nfl.com/player/bobbythompson/2527311/profile |url-status=dead }}</ref> and, before that, in the [[Canadian Football League]] (CFL) for the [[Saskatchewan Roughriders]].

Thompson served as an executive with the [[Stars Football League]] (SFL), a league founded and managed by his former agent, Peter Hulthwaite, throughout that league's existence.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://starsfootballleague.com/about/|title = About | Stars Pro Spring Football League}}</ref>

Brown was also a member of the [[Southern California Sun]] of the [[World Football League]] (WFL). ==Early life== Booker Taylor Brown was born on September 25, 1952, in [[Wesson, Mississippi]].{{cite web | url=http://www.profootballarchives.com/players/b/brow02400.html | title=BOOKER BROWN | publisher=Pro Football Archives | accessdate=29 December 2024}} He attended [[Santa Barbara High School]] in [[Santa Barbara, California]], where he played football, basketball, and baseball. He was a [[Lineman (American football)|lineman]] in football and a [[first baseman]] in [[baseball]]. ==College career== Brown first played [[college football]] at [[Santa Barbara City College]] from 1970 to 1971.{{cite web | url=http://californiacommunitycolleges.cccco.edu/Newsroom/NotableAlumni/NFLAlumni.aspx | title=NFL Alumni | publisher=californiacommunitycolleges.cccco.edu | accessdate=August 20, 2014 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131019045813/http://californiacommunitycolleges.cccco.edu/Newsroom/NotableAlumni/NFLAlumni.aspx | archive-date=October 19, 2013 | url-status=dead }} In 2019, Brown was inducted into the Santa Barbara City College Athletics Hall of Fame as a member of their inaugural class.{{cite web | url=https://www.sbccvaqueros.com/hall_of_fame/HOFers | title=SBCC Vaqueros Hall of Famers – Santa Barbara City College }} He was a two-year [[letterman (sports)|letterman]] for the [[USC Trojans football|USC Trojans]] of the [[University of Southern California]] from 1972 to 1973. The [[1972 USC Trojans football team|1972 Trojans]] were consensus national champions. Brown was a consensus [[College Football All-America Team|All-American]] in [[1973 NCAA Division I football season|1973]].{{cite web|title=2014 NCAA Football Records: Consensus All-America Selections|publisher=National Collegiate Athletic Association (NCAA)|year=2014|accessdate=August 16, 2014|page=6|url=http://fs.ncaa.org/Docs/stats/football_records/2014/Awards.pdf|archive-date=November 26, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181126094941/http://fs.ncaa.org/Docs/stats/football_records/2014/awards.pdf|url-status=dead}}{{cite web | url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/players/booker-brown-1.html | title=Booker Brown | publisher=Sports Reference LLC | work=sports-reference.com | accessdate=August 20, 2014}} ==Professional career== Brown was selected by the [[Houston Oilers]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL) in the sixth round, with the 154th overall pick, of the [[1974 NFL draft]], and by the [[Southern California Sun]] of the [[World Football League]] (WFL) in the third round, with the 31st overall pick, of the [[1974 WFL draft]]. He decided to sign with the Sun and was a member of the team during the [[1974 WFL season]].{{cite web | url=http://www.nasljerseys.com/WFL/Players/B/Brown.Booker.htm | title=Booker Brown | publisher=nasljerseys.com | accessdate=August 20, 2014}} On May 29, 1975, the Oilers traded the rights to Brown and [[Benny Johnson (American football)|Benny Johnson]] to the [[San Diego Chargers]] for [[Carl Mauck]].{{cite web | url=https://prosportstransactions.com/football/Search/SearchResults.php?Player=Booker+Brown&Team=&BeginDate=&EndDate=&PlayerMovementChkBx=yes&submit=Search | title=Search Results | publisher=prosportstransactions.com | accessdate=29 December 2024}} Brown signed with the Chargers on June 20, 1975. He played in 11 games, starting seven, for the Chargers during the 1975 season, recording one fumble recovery. The next year, he was placed on the reserve/non-football illness list on June 20, 1976. He appeared in six games, starting one, in 1977.{{cite web | url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/B/BrowBo20.htm | title=Booker Brown | publisher=[[Pro Football Reference]] | accessdate=29 December 2024}} On August 4, 1978, Brown was traded to the [[Tampa Bay Buccaneers]] for a 1980 fourth round draft pick. He was placed on injured reserve on August 30, 1978, and spent the entire season there. He was released by the Buccaneers on August 21, 1979.{{cite web | url=http://www.profootballarchives.com/transactions/b/brow02400.html | title=Booker Brown NFL Transactions | publisher=Pro Football Archives | accessdate=29 December 2024}} ==Personal life== Brown was later a pastor and also founded a charitable organization. He died on July 18, 2022, in [[Mojave, California]] after an extended illness.{{cite web | url=https://www.independent.com/2022/07/25/booker-brown-santa-barbara-high-athletic-legend-dies-at-69/ | title=Booker Brown, Santa Barbara High Athletic Legend, Dies at 69 | date=July 25, 2022 }} ==References== {{reflist}} ==External links== *[http://www.justsportsstats.com/footballstatsindex.php?player_id=brownboo001 Stats Crew profile] {{1972 USC Trojans football navbox}} {{1973 College Football Consensus All-Americans}} {{Houston Oilers 1974 draft navbox}} {{DEFAULTSORT:Brown, Booker}} [[Category:1952 births]] [[Category:2022 deaths]] [[Category:Players of American football from Mississippi]] [[Category:American football offensive tackles]] [[Category:USC Trojans football players]] [[Category:Southern California Sun players]] [[Category:San Diego Chargers players]] [[Category:All-American college football players]] [[Category:People from Wesson, Mississippi]] [[Category:Santa Barbara City Vaqueros football players]] [[Category:20th-century African-American sportsmen]] [[Category:20th-century American sportsmen]] [[Category:Tampa Bay Buccaneers players]]

'''Bobby Marcellous McCain''' (born August 18, 1993) is an American professional [[American football|football]] [[safety (gridiron football position)|safety]]. He played [[college football]] for the [[Memphis Tigers football|Memphis Tigers]] and was drafted by the [[Miami Dolphins]] in the fifth round of the [[2015 NFL draft]]. McCain has also played for the [[Washington Commanders|Washington Football Team / Commanders]] and [[New York Giants]].

==Early life==
McCain was born on August 18, 1993, in [[Sylacauga, Alabama]]. He attended [[Oxford High School (Alabama)|Oxford High School]], where he played [[high school football|football]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Inabinett |first=Mark |date=May 2, 2015 |title=Oxford's Bobby McCain drafted by Miami Dolphins |url=https://www.al.com/sports/2015/05/oxfords_bobby_mccain_selected.html |access-date=March 21, 2021 |website=AL.com |language=en}}</ref> McCain was considered a three-star recruit by [[Rivals.com]] and was listed as the No. 36 prospect from the state of Alabama in 2011. He committed to [[Memphis Tigers football|Memphis]] to play college football over offers from [[Auburn Tigers football|Auburn]], [[Kentucky Wildcats football|Kentucky]], [[Mississippi State Bulldogs football|Mississippi State]], and [[Tennessee Volunteers football|Tennessee]], among others.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Bobby McCain, 2011 Cornerback - Rivals.com |url=https://n.rivals.com/content/prospects/2011/bobby-mccain-35425 |access-date=March 21, 2021 |website=n.rivals.com}}</ref>

==College career==
McCain played his college career at the [[University of Memphis]] where he was a four-year starter at and had 12 career [[interceptions]], including 11 in his final two years.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Bobby McCain College Stats, School, Draft, Gamelog, Splits |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/players/bobby-mccain-1.html |access-date=March 21, 2021 |website=College Football at Sports-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref>

===Miami Dolphins===
==== 2015 ====
The [[Miami Dolphins]] selected McCain in the fifth round with the 145th overall pick in the [[2015 NFL draft]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=2015 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2015/draft.htm |access-date=March 21, 2021 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> McCain was the 18th cornerback drafted in 2015.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Kelly |first=Omar |date=May 2, 2015 |title=Dolphins lead off fifth-round flurry to close out draft, picking Memphis CB Bobby McCain |url=https://www.sun-sentinel.com/sports/miami-dolphins/sfl-miami-dolphins-bobby-mccain-20150502-story.html |access-date=March 21, 2021 |website=South Florida Sun-Sentinel}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Neal |first=David J. |date=May 10, 2015 |title=Miami Dolphins rookie Bobby McCain has lofty goals |url=https://www.miamiherald.com/sports/nfl/miami-dolphins/article20640546.html |access-date=March 21, 2021 |website=Miami Herald}}</ref> On May 7, 2015, the Dolphins signed McCain to a four-year, $2.50 million contract that includes a [[signing bonus]] of $228,288.<ref name="spotrac">{{Cite web |title=Spotrac.com: Bobby McCain contract |url=https://www.spotrac.com/nfl/miami-dolphins/bobby-mccain-16871/ |access-date=October 9, 2018 |website=Spotrac.com}}</ref>

Throughout [[Training camp (NFL)|training camp]], McCain competed to be a starting cornerback against [[Jamar Taylor]], [[Tony Lippett]], [[Brice McCain]], and [[Will Davis (cornerback)|Will Davis]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=July 29, 2015 |title=Dolphins bubble watch: Will Davis and other talented defensive backs in tight competition |url=http://dailydolphin.blog.palmbeachpost.com/2015/07/28/dolphins-bubble-watch-will-davis-and-other-talented-secondary-players-in-tight-competition/ |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150729151631/http://dailydolphin.blog.palmbeachpost.com/2015/07/28/dolphins-bubble-watch-will-davis-and-other-talented-secondary-players-in-tight-competition/ |archive-date=July 29, 2015 |access-date=October 9, 2018 |website=Palm Beach Post}}</ref> Head coach [[Joe Philbin]] named McCain the fourth cornerback on the depth chart to begin the regular season, behind [[Brent Grimes]], Taylor, and Davis.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Nogle, Kevin |date=September 5, 2015 |title=Dolphins depth chart 2015: Projecting the Miami depth chart after final roster cuts |url=https://www.thephinsider.com/2015/9/5/9267053/dolphins-depth-chart-2015-projecting-the-miami-depth-chart-after |access-date=October 9, 2018 |website=thephinsider.com}}</ref>

He made his professional regular season debut in the Dolphins season-opening 17–10 win at the [[Washington Redskins]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Miami Dolphins at Washington Redskins – September 13th, 2015 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201509130was.htm |access-date=March 21, 2021 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> On October 5, 2015, the Dolphins fired head coach Joe Philbin after they began the season with a 1–3 record. Tight ends coach [[Dan Campbell]] was named the interim head coach for the remainder of the season.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Walker |first=James |date=October 5, 2015 |title=Dolphins fire coach Joe Philbin after team stumbles to 1–3 start |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/13814560/miami-dolphins-fire-joe-philbin |access-date=October 10, 2018 |website=ESPN.com}}</ref> On December 6, 2015, he collected a season-high seven solo [[Tackle (football move)#Gridiron football|tackles]] and deflected a pass in the Dolphins' 15–13 victory against the [[Baltimore Ravens]] in Week 13.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Baltimore Ravens at Miami Dolphins – December 6th, 2015 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201512060mia.htm |access-date=March 21, 2021 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> He finished his rookie season in 2015 with 28 combined tackles (23 solo) and four [[pass deflections]] in 16 games and four starts.<ref name="career">{{Cite web |title=NFL Player stats: Bobby McCain (career) |url=https://www.nfl.com/player/bobbymccain/2552434/careerstats |access-date=October 9, 2018 |website=NFL.com}}</ref>

==== 2016 ====
On January 9, 2016, the Dolphins hired [[Chicago Bears]] offensive coordinator [[Adam Gase]] as their new head coach.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Sessler |first=Marc |date=January 9, 2016 |title=Miami Dolphins hire Adam Gase as new head coach |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/miami-dolphins-hire-adam-gase-as-new-head-coach-0ap3000000619758 |access-date=October 10, 2018 |website=NFL.com}}</ref> McCain entered training camp as the first-team [[nickelback (gridiron football)|nickelback]], but saw competition for his role from [[Jordan Lucas]] and [[Tyler Patmon]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Abramson |first=Andrew |date=June 6, 2016 |title=Porous Miami Dolphins secondary counting on rookie Xavien Howard |url=https://www.mypalmbeachpost.com/sports/football/porous-miami-dolphins-secondary-counting-rookie-xavien-howard/PUjglsETCw2Hd9k5qoYy1K/ |access-date=October 10, 2018 |website=mypalmbeachpost.com }}{{Dead link|date=June 2024 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref> Head coach Adam Gase named McCain the third cornerback on the Dolphins' depth chart to begin the regular season, behind [[Byron Maxwell]] and rookie [[Xavien Howard]]. He was also named the first-team nickelback.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Nogle |first=Kevin |date=September 6, 2016 |title=Dolphins depth chart 2016: Arian Foster named starting running back, Laremy Tunsil left guard |url=https://www.thephinsider.com/2016/9/6/12811924/dolphins-depth-chart-2016-arian-foster-laremy-tunsil-devante-parker-jarvis-landry |access-date=October 10, 2018 |website=thephinsider.com}}</ref>

On September 29, 2016, McCain recorded four combined tackles, deflected a pass, and made his first career [[Quarterback sack|sack]] on [[Andy Dalton]] during a 22–7 loss at the [[Cincinnati Bengals]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Miami Dolphins at Cincinnati Bengals – September 29th, 2016 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201609290cin.htm |access-date=March 21, 2021 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> On November 6, 2016, McCain recorded three solo tackles, broke up a pass, and made his first career interception in the Dolphins' 27–23 win against the [[New York Jets]] in Week 9. McCain intercepted a pass by New York Jets' quarterback [[Ryan Fitzpatrick]], that was originally intended for tight end [[Austin Seferian-Jenkins]], and returned it for a 17-yard gain in the third quarter.<ref>{{Cite web |title=New York Jets at Miami Dolphins – November 6th, 2016 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201611060mia.htm |access-date=March 21, 2021 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> In Week 12, he collected a season-high five combined tackles and broke up one pass during a 31–24 victory against the [[San Francisco 49ers]] in Week 12.<ref>{{Cite web |title=San Francisco 49ers at Miami Dolphins – November 27th, 2016 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201611270mia.htm |access-date=March 21, 2021 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> He finished the [[2016 NFL season]] with 45 combined tackles (32 solo), six pass deflections, one interception, one sack, and a forced [[fumble]] in 16 games and eight starts.<ref name="career" />

The Dolphins finished second in the [[AFC East]] with a 10–6 record and earned a Wild Card berth.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2016 NFL Standings & Team Stats |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2016/index.htm |access-date=March 21, 2021 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> On January 8, 2017, McCain started in his first career playoff game and recorded two tackles as the Dolphins lost the [[American Football Conference|AFC]] wild card game 30–12 at the [[Pittsburgh Steelers]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Wild Card – Miami Dolphins at Pittsburgh Steelers – January 8th, 2017 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201701080pit.htm |access-date=March 21, 2021 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

==== 2017 ====
On January 12, 2017, the Dolphins announced their decision to promote linebackers coach [[Matt Burke (American football)|Matt Burke]] to defensive coordinator after [[Vance Joseph]] accepted the head coaching position with the [[Denver Broncos]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Rapp |first=Timothy |date=January 12, 2017 |title=Matt Burke Named Dolphins DC: Latest Contract Details, Comments and Reaction |url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2686732-matt-burke-named-dolphins-dc-latest-contract-details-comments-and-reaction |access-date=October 10, 2018 |website=BleacherReport.com}}</ref> During training camp, McCain competed to retain his position at nickelback against Tony Lippett, Michael Thomas, [[Cordrea Tankersley]], [[Alterraun Verner]], Jordan Lucas, and [[Lafayette Pitts]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Turner |first=Derric |date=August 3, 2017 |title=Bobby McCain looking to compete for starting nickel spot |url=https://phinphanatic.com/2017/08/03/bobby-mccain-looking-compete-starting-nickel-spot/ |access-date=October 10, 2018 |website=phinphanatic.com}}</ref> Head coach Adam Gase named McCain the first-team nickelback to start the season, behind Byron Maxwell and Xavien Howard.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Ourlads.com: Miami Dolphins Depth Chart: 10/01/2017 |url=https://www.ourlads.com/nfldepthcharts/archive/200/MIA |access-date=October 10, 2018 |website=Ourlads.com}}</ref>

On November 26, 2017, during Week 12 against the [[New England Patriots]], McCain was ejected for throwing a punch at [[wide receiver]] [[Danny Amendola]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=November 26, 2017 |title=Bobby McCain ejected for throwing punch |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/dolphins-cb-bobby-mccain-ejected-for-throwing-punch-0ap3000000882928 |access-date=November 26, 2017 |publisher=NFL}}</ref> In Week 16, he collected a season-high eight combined tackles and broke up a pass during a 29–13 loss at the [[Kansas City Chiefs]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Miami Dolphins at Kansas City Chiefs – December 24th, 2017 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201712240kan.htm |access-date=March 21, 2021 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> McCain finished the season with 48 combined tackles (36 solo), seven pass deflections, two interceptions, and a sack in 16 games and seven starts.<ref name="career" />

==== 2018 ====
On June 1, 2018, McCain signed a four-year, $27 million contract extension with the Dolphins with $13 million guaranteed.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Wesseling |first=Chris |date=June 1, 2018 |title=Dolphins sign Bobby McCain for four years, $27 million |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/dolphins-sign-bobby-mccain-for-four-years-27-million-0ap3000000935409 |website=NFL.com}}</ref> During training camp, McCain competed to be a starting cornerback against Cordrea Tankersley. Head coach Adam Gase named McCain and Xavien Howard the starting cornerbacks to begin the regular season in 2018.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Nogle |first=Kevin |date=September 3, 2018 |title=Predicting the Dolphins' depth chart 2018: 53-man roster edition |url=https://www.thephinsider.com/2018/9/3/17815364/miami-dolphins-depth-chart-prediction-53-man-roster-cuts-complete |access-date=October 10, 2018 |website=thephinsider.com}}</ref> Overall, McCain finished the 2018 season with 61 total tackles, two sacks, one interception, and five passes defended.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Bobby McCain 2018 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/M/McCaBo01.htm |access-date=March 21, 2021 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

====2019====
In Week 3 against the [[Dallas Cowboys]], McCain recorded his first interception of the season off [[Dak Prescott]] in the 31–6 loss.<ref>{{Cite web |date=September 22, 2019 |title=Prescott, Cowboys get out of funk, ease past Dolphins 31–6 |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/recap?gameId=401127921 |access-date=September 22, 2019 |website=[[ESPN]] |agency=Associated Press}}</ref> On November 20, 2019, McCain was placed on [[injured reserve]], ending his season.<ref>{{Cite web |date=November 20, 2019 |title=Dolphins Sign Adrian Colbert, Activate Andrew Van Ginkel, Promote Gerald Willis |url=https://www.miamidolphins.com/news/dolphins-sign-adrian-colbert-activate-andrew-van-ginkel-promote-gerald-willis |access-date=March 21, 2021 |website=MiamiDolphins.com}}</ref> In nine games, he finished with 25 total tackles, two interceptions, and three passes defended.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Bobby McCain 2019 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/M/McCaBo01/gamelog/2019/ |access-date=March 21, 2021 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

====2020====
In the 2020 season, McCain played in all 16 regular season games, of which he started 15. He finished with 46 total tackles, one interception, and five passes defended.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Bobby McCain 2020 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/M/McCaBo01/gamelog/2020/ |access-date=March 21, 2021 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> McCain was released by the Dolphins on May 6, 2021.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Kelly |first=Omar |date=May 6, 2021 |title=Dolphins release veteran safety and team captain Bobby McCain |url=https://www.sun-sentinel.com/sports/miami-dolphins/fl-sp-dolphins-bobby-mccain-released-20210506-hi3hmdtwsng7ngkiuwplr3keru-story.html |access-date=May 6, 2021 |website=Sun-Sentinel.com |language=en}}</ref>

===Washington Football Team / Commanders===
[[File:Bobby McCain & Evan Engram WFT@NYG JAN2022.jpg|thumb|right|McCain with an interception against the New York Giants in 2021]]
McCain signed a one-year contract with the [[Washington Football Team]] on May 17, 2021.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Keim |first=John |date=2021-05-14 |title=WFT signs ex-Dolphins S McCain to 1-year deal |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/31445749/washington-signs-former-miami-dolphins-safety-bobby-mccain-1-year-deal |access-date=2023-07-17 |website=ESPN.com |language=en}}</ref> McCain recorded his first interception of the season against [[Kansas City Chiefs]] quarterback [[Patrick Mahomes]] in Week 6.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Palmer |first=Tod |date=2021-10-17 |title=Chiefs QB Patrick Mahomes on 'C'mon, Man' interception: 'That's bad' |url=https://www.kshb.com/sports/chiefs-qb-patrick-mahomes-on-cmon-man-interception-thats-bad |access-date=2023-07-17 |website=KSHB 41 Kansas City News |language=en}}</ref> In the Week 10 win over the [[Tampa Bay Buccaneers]], McCain intercepted [[Tom Brady]] in the first half of the game.<ref>{{cite web|work=WashingtonFootball.com|url=https://www.washingtonfootball.com/news/5-takeaways-washington-buccaneers-week-10|title=5 takeaways from Washington upsetting the Buccaneers|date=November 14, 2021|accessdate=November 21, 2021|first=Zach|last=Selby}}</ref> He recorded two interceptions against [[New York Giants]] quarterback [[Jake Fromm]] in the final game of the season and returned one of them for his first career touchdown.<ref>{{cite web|work=Commanders.com|url=https://www.commanders.com/news/3-game-balls-washington-giants-week-18|title=Game Balls {{!}} 4 standouts after Washington's season finale win|date=January 9, 2022|accessdate=March 16, 2022|first=Hannah|last=Lichtenstein}}</ref> In the 2021 season, McCain appeared in 17 games and started 16. He finished with 63 total tackles, four interceptions, and nine passes defended.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Bobby McCain 2021 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/M/McCaBo01/gamelog/2021/ |access-date=2023-07-17 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

McCain re-signed with the team on a two-year, $11 million contract on March 17, 2022.<ref>{{Cite web |date=March 17, 2022 |title=Commanders re-sign multiple players |url=https://www.commanders.com/news/commanders-re-sign-multiple-players |access-date=March 17, 2022 |website=Commanders.com}}</ref> McCain would play [[slot cornerback]] later in the season.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Manning |first=Bryan |date=2022-11-20 |title=Bobby McCain is now the Commanders' slot corner |url=https://commanderswire.usatoday.com/2022/11/20/washington-defensive-back-bobby-mccain-is-now-the-washington-commanders-slot-corner/ |access-date=2023-07-17 |website=Commanders Wire|publisher=USA Today |language=en-US}}</ref> In the 2022 season, McCain appeared in all 17 games and started 16. He finished with 76 total tackles, five passes defended, and one forced fumble.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Bobby McCain 2022 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/M/McCaBo01/gamelog/2022/ |access-date=2023-07-17 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> He was released on February 27, 2023.<ref>{{Cite web |date=February 27, 2023 |title=Commanders release Carson Wentz and Bobby McCain |url=https://www.commanders.com/news/commanders-release-carson-wentz-and-bobby-mccain |access-date=February 27, 2023 |website=Commanders.com |archive-date=February 27, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230227203500/https://www.commanders.com/news/commanders-release-carson-wentz-and-bobby-mccain |url-status=dead }}</ref>

===New York Giants===
On March 23, 2023, McCain signed a one-year contract with the Giants.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Salomone |first=Dan |date=March 23, 2023 |title=Giants sign S Bobby McCain; 5 things to know |url=https://www.giants.com/news/bobby-mccain-contract-washington-commanders-miami-dolphins-free-agency-memphis |access-date=2023-07-17 |website=Giants.com}}</ref> He was waived on December 17, 2023.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.giants.com/news/darren-waller-activated-injured-reserve-week-15-new-orleans-saints-bobby-mccain|work=Giants.com|title=Darren Waller activated from injured reserve|date=December 17, 2023|accessdate=January 3, 2024|first=Dan|last=Salomone}}</ref>

'''Bobby Richardson''' (born November 30, 1992) is an American former professional [[Gridiron football|football]] player who was a [[defensive end]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He was signed by the [[New Orleans Saints]] as an [[undrafted free agent]] in 2015.<ref>[http://www.nola.com/saints/index.ssf/2015/08/bobby_richardson.html Undrafted Saints rookie Bobby Richardson 'doesn't want to fall into the crowd']</ref><ref>[https://www.espn.com/blog/new-orleans-saints/post/_/id/16696/undrafted-saints-rookie-bobby-richardson-doesnt-want-to-waste-opportunity Undrafted Saints rookie Bobby Richardson doesn't want to waste opportunity]</ref> He played [[college football]] for the [[Indiana Hoosiers football|Indiana Hoosiers]].

==Professional career==
===New Orleans Saints===
Richardson signed with the [[New Orleans Saints]] as an undrafted rookie free agent in 2015. Richardson started 2015 as a starting [[defensive end]] for the Saints. In the Saints' Week 15 matchup against the [[Jacksonville Jaguars]], Richardson recorded his first career [[interception]]. Saints cornerback [[Delvin Breaux]] tipped a ball thrown by Jaguar quarterback [[Blake Bortles]] and it flew through the air, allowing Richardson to catch it. On September 3, 2016, he was waived by the Saints.<ref>{{cite web|title=After cuts, New Orleans Saints have first 53-man roster of 2016|url=http://www.nola.com/saints/index.ssf/2016/09/live_new_orleans_saints_start.html|last=Katzenstein|first=Josh|website=NOLA.com}}</ref> He was then signed to the Saints' practice squad. On September 14, 2016, he was released from their practice squad.<ref>{{cite web|title=New Orleans Saints release RB C.J. Spiller|url=http://www.neworleanssaints.com/news-and-events/article-1/New-Orleans-Saints-release-RB-CJ-Spiller/3ffb39a6-4c80-4c9a-8b77-c93604f5d3cb|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170918064220/http://www.neworleanssaints.com/news-and-events/article-1/New-Orleans-Saints-release-RB-CJ-Spiller/3ffb39a6-4c80-4c9a-8b77-c93604f5d3cb|url-status=dead|archive-date=September 18, 2017|website=NewOrleansSaints.com|date=September 14, 2016}}</ref>

===Washington Redskins===
On September 19, 2016, Richardson was signed to the [[Washington Redskins]]' practice squad.<ref>{{cite web|title=Kedric Golston Placed On Injured Reserve, Matt Ioannidis On Active Roster|url=http://www.redskins.com/news/article-1/Kedric-Golston-Placed-On-Injured-Reserve-Matt-Ioannidis-On-Active-Roster/1113255d-e6c2-4514-bd73-eb73b5842d6c|last=Czarda|first=Stephen|website=Redskins.com|access-date=2016-09-19|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160920132401/http://www.redskins.com/news/article-1/Kedric-Golston-Placed-On-Injured-Reserve-Matt-Ioannidis-On-Active-Roster/1113255d-e6c2-4514-bd73-eb73b5842d6c|archive-date=2016-09-20|url-status=dead}}</ref> He was released on October 19, 2016.<ref>{{cite web|title=10/19: Redskins Make Roster Moves|url=http://www.redskins.com/news/article-1/1019-Redskins-Make-Roster-Moves/90ad116f-4dd2-453f-8982-3ddc8a713131|website=Redskins.com|date=October 19, 2016|access-date=October 20, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161020110215/http://www.redskins.com/news/article-1/1019-Redskins-Make-Roster-Moves/90ad116f-4dd2-453f-8982-3ddc8a713131|archive-date=October 20, 2016|url-status=dead}}</ref>

===Kansas City Chiefs===
Richardson was signed to the [[Kansas City Chiefs]] practice squad on October 26, 2016. He was released on November 9, 2016.

===Denver Broncos===
On February 24, 2017, Richardson signed with the Broncos.<ref>{{cite web|title=Broncos sign DE Bobby Richardson|url=http://www.denverbroncos.com/news-and-blogs/article-1/Broncos-sign-DE-Bobby-Richardson/84b5f737-8fdc-4067-b6f3-3883723f45e6|author=Mason, Andrew|website=Broncos.com|date=February 24, 2017|access-date=February 24, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170225054204/http://www.denverbroncos.com/news-and-blogs/article-1/Broncos-sign-DE-Bobby-Richardson/84b5f737-8fdc-4067-b6f3-3883723f45e6|archive-date=February 25, 2017|url-status=dead}}</ref> On May 3, 2017, Richardson was waived by the Broncos.<ref>{{cite web|title=Broncos re-sign defensive end Billy Winn, waive Bobby Richardson|url=http://www.denverbroncos.com/news-and-blogs/article-1/Broncos-re-sign-defensive-end-Billy-Winn-waive-Bobby-Richardson/b4f612be-2858-433e-9d9e-802cde1377ec|author=Swanson, Ben|website=DenverBroncos.com|date=May 3, 2017|access-date=May 3, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170504011800/http://www.denverbroncos.com/news-and-blogs/article-1/Broncos-re-sign-defensive-end-Billy-Winn-waive-Bobby-Richardson/b4f612be-2858-433e-9d9e-802cde1377ec|archive-date=May 4, 2017|url-status=dead}}</ref>

===New York Giants===
On August 15, 2017, Richardson signed with the [[New York Giants]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Giants sign Bobby Richardson, place Corbin Bryant on IR|url=http://profootballtalk.nbcsports.com/2017/08/15/giants-sign-bobby-richardson-place-corbin-bryant-on-ir/|author=Alper, Josh|website=ProFootballTalk.NBCSports.com|date=August 15, 2017}}</ref> He was waived on September 2, 2017.<ref>{{cite web|title=New York Giants announce 2017 53-man roster|url=http://www.giants.com/news-and-blogs/article-1/New-York-Giants-announce-2017-53-man-roster/af61460d-cd5a-4723-95d7-e08c74eaf74e|author=Eisen, Michael|website=Giants.com|date=September 2, 2017|url-status=dead|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20171205020739/http://www.giants.com/news-and-blogs/article-1/New-York-Giants-announce-2017-53-man-roster/af61460d-cd5a-4723-95d7-e08c74eaf74e|archivedate=December 5, 2017}}</ref>

===Hamilton Tiger-Cats===
Richardson signed with the [[Hamilton Tiger-Cats]] of the [[Canadian Football League]] on April 20, 2018.<ref>{{cite news |title=Tiger-Cats Sign Five International Players |url=https://ticats.ca/tiger-cats-sign-five-international-players/ |website=TiCats.ca |date=April 20, 2018 |accessdate=February 27, 2020}}</ref> He re-signed with the team on December 6, 2018,<ref>{{cite news |title=Five Players Re-Sign with Tiger-Cats |url=https://ticats.ca/five-players-re-sign-with-tiger-cats/ |website=December 6, 2018 |accessdate=February 27, 2020}}</ref> but retired on May 6, 2019.<ref>{{cite news |title=Tiger-Cats Release 14, Richardson Retires |url=https://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/tiger-cats-release-14-richardson-retires/n-5482659 |website=OurSportsCentral.com |date=May 6, 2019 |accessdate=February 27, 2020}}</ref>

===Tampa Bay Vipers===
In October 2019, Richardson was among the [[Tampa Bay Vipers]]' open-round choices in the [[2020 XFL draft]].<ref>{{cite web|last=Talbot|first=Damond|url=https://www.nfldraftdiamonds.com/2019/10/xfl-draft-8/|title=XFL Draft Phase 5: The Final Rounds of the Draft, Find out who was selected|publisher=NFL Draft Diamonds|date=October 16, 2019|accessdate=October 23, 2019}}</ref> He had his contract terminated when the league suspended operations on April 10, 2020.<ref>{{cite news |author=Condotta, Bob |title=XFL suspends operations, terminates all employees, but Jim Zorn says he has hopes league will continue |url=https://www.seattletimes.com/sports/xfl-suspends-operations-terminates-all-employees/ |website=SeattleTimes.com |date=April 10, 2020 |accessdate=July 17, 2020}}</ref>

'''Bobby Williams''' (February 28, 1942 – August 10, 2012)  was an American professional [[American football|football]] player who played five seasons in the [[National Football League]] (NFL), for the [[St. Louis Cardinals (NFL)|St. Louis Cardinals]] and the [[Detroit Lions]]. Williams was mostly known as a return specialist, and at different times in his career also played running back and defensive back.<ref name="UCO" /><ref name="Tributes">{{cite web |url= http://newsok.com/article/3700608 |title=Tributes |work=newsok.com |date=August 13, 2012 |accessdate=December 24, 2016}}</ref>

==Early life==
Williams was born in [[Geiger, Alabama]] and grew up in [[Lincoln, Nebraska]]. He attended [[Lincoln High School (Lincoln, Nebraska)|Lincoln High School]] where he participated in a variety of sports. He set Nebraska state records in the 100 yard dash and the [[long jump]], the latter of which was later broken by [[Gale Sayers]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://dataomaha.com/neb100/player/37 |title=Bobby Williams |work=Omaha-World Herald |accessdate=December 24, 2016}}</ref> He would attend [[University of Central Oklahoma|Central State College]] in [[Edmond, Oklahoma]]. He played running back on the [[Central Oklahoma Bronchos football|Central State Bronchos]] football team. He had 3,094 all-purpose yards, and still holds the school record for kick return yards at 1,063.<ref name="Tributes" /> He also helped the Bronchos win the 1962 [[NAIA football national championship|NAIA Football National Championship]].

==NFL career==
Williams was drafted by the [[Arizona Cardinals|St. Louis Cardinals]] in the 11th round and 163rd pick overall of the [[1966 NFL draft]].<ref name="NFL">{{cite web |url= https://www.nfl.com/player/bobbywilliams/2528850/profile |title=Bobby Williams, DB|work=NFL.com |accessdate=December 24, 2016}}</ref> He spent two years in St. Louis, before being traded to the [[Detroit Lions]]. He would play with the Lions for three more seasons. He would finish with 3 interceptions, and 2 kickoff return touchdowns.

'''Jesus "Bobo" Wilson''' (born January 25, 1995) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[wide receiver]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Florida State Seminoles football|Florida State Seminoles]], and was signed by the [[Tampa Bay Buccaneers]] as an undrafted free agent in 2017.

'''Boston Nealand Scott''' (born April 27, 1995) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] [[running back]] and professional ''[[Rocket League]]'' [[esports]] player and streamer for [[Dignitas (esports)|Dignitas]]. He played [[college football]] at [[Louisiana Tech Bulldogs football|Louisiana Tech]]. He was selected by the [[New Orleans Saints]] in the sixth round of the [[2018 NFL draft]]. Scott also played for the [[Philadelphia Eagles]] and was known among fans as "'''the Giant Killer'''" due to his propensity to perform well against the [[New York Giants]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Kaye |first=Mike |date=November 24, 2021 |title=How Eagles' Boston Scott earned 'Giant Killer' nickname over past 2 seasons |url=https://nj.com/eagles/2021/11/how-eagles-boston-scott-earned-giant-killer-nickname-over-past-2-seasons.html |access-date=March 5, 2023 |website=NJ.com}}</ref>

==Early life==
Scott attended [[Zachary High School]] where he was the leading rusher and earned local and state honors.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://zacharybroncofootball.com/ |title=Zachary Bronco Football |website=zacharybroncofootball.com |access-date=December 11, 2017}}</ref> He was a high school state champion in [[Powerlifting|weightlifting]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://powerlifting.zacharyhigh.org/ |title=Powerlifting |website=powerlifting.zacharyhigh.org |access-date=December 11, 2017}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=November 16, 2017 |title=Louisiana Tech's Boston Scott is the Most Elusive Player You've Never Heard Of |url=https://herosports.com/film-room-louisiana-tech-football-boston-scott-ahah/ |access-date=March 5, 2023 |website=HERO Sports |language=en-US}}</ref>

==College career==
[[File:Boston Scott 6 LaTech (cropped).jpg|thumb|Scott in 2017]]
Scott played four seasons for [[Louisiana Tech Bulldogs football|Louisiana Tech]]. In his senior season at Louisiana Tech, he rushed for 937 yards on 163 attempts, resulting in a regular season average of 5.7 yards per attempt. In 2017, he had 1,301 yards of overall offense, contributing 108.4 yards per game.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Conference USA – 2017 Football Overall Statistics |url=http://www.conferenceusa.com/stats.aspx?path=football&year=2017& |access-date=December 11, 2017 |website=Conference USA}}</ref> Scott was a watchlist candidate for the [[Wuerffel Trophy]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=July 18, 2017 |title=College football: 2017 Danny Wuerffel Award watch list |url=https://www.ncaa.com/news/football/article/2017-07-18/college-football-2017-danny-wuerffel-award-watch-list |access-date=December 12, 2017 |website=NCAA.com}}</ref>

Scott was selected by the [[New Orleans Saints]] in the sixth round (201st overall) of the [[2018 NFL draft]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Morale III |first=Amos |date=April 28, 2018 |title=Saints take Louisiana Tech running back Boston Scott with 2nd sixth-round pick |url=https://www.nola.com/saints/index.ssf/2018/04/saints_take_lousiaina_tech_run.html |access-date=June 30, 2018 |website=NOLA.com}}</ref> On May 10, 2018, Scott signed his rookie contract with the Saints.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.neworleanssaints.com/news/new-orleans-saints-sign-six-draft-picks-20646723 |title=New Orleans Saints sign six draft picks |date=May 10, 2018 |website=NewOrleansSaints.com |access-date=May 24, 2018}}</ref> After making the Saints' initial 53-man roster, he was waived on September 5, and was re-signed to the [[practice squad]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.neworleanssaints.com/news/boston-scott-s-release-allowed-new-orleans-saints-to-address-other-positions#FB |title=Boston Scott's release allowed New Orleans Saints to address other positions |date=September 6, 2018 |website=NewOrleansSaints.com |access-date=September 6, 2018}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Sigler |first=John |date=September 6, 2018 |title=Saints rookie RB Boston Scott clears waivers, joins practice squad |url=https://saintswire.usatoday.com/2018/09/06/saints-rookie-rb-boston-scott-clears-waivers-joins-practice-squad/ |access-date=March 4, 2023 |website=Saints Wire |publisher=USA Today}}</ref>

On August 30, 2024, the [[Pittsburgh Steelers]] signed Scott to their practice squad.<ref name="Steelers20240830">{{cite web|url=https://www.steelers.com/news/steelers-sign-seven-to-practice-squad|title=Steelers sign eight to practice squad|last=Varley|first=Teresa|website=Steelers.com|date=August 30, 2024|access-date=September 2, 2024}}</ref> He was released on September 13.<ref name="j669">{{cite web | last=Campbell | first=Dominic | title=Report: Steelers Cut Former Eagles RB | website=SI.com| date=2024-09-13 | url=https://www.si.com/nfl/steelers/news/report-pittsburgh-steelers-cut-former-philadelphia-eagles-rb-boston-scott | access-date=2025-01-08}}</ref>

On March 18, 2026, after spending the entire 2025 season unsigned, Scott announced his retirement from professional football.<ref>{{cite web |date=March 18, 2026 |title=Boston Scott announces his retirement |url=https://www.philadelphiaeagles.com/news/boston-scott-announces-his-retirement-eagles |access-date=21 March 2026 |website=PhiladelphiaEagles.com}}</ref>

'''Robert Nnanna Okereke''' ({{IPAc-en|oʊ|k|ə|r|ə|ˈ|k|eɪ}} {{respell|oh|kər|ə|KAY}};<ref>{{cite web |title=2022 Indianapolis Colts Media Guide |url=https://static.www.nfl.com/league/apps/league-site/media-guides/2022/IND.pdf |website=NFL.com |publisher=National Football League |access-date=October 7, 2022}}</ref> born July 29, 1996) is an American professional [[American football|football]] [[linebacker]]. He played [[college football]] for the [[Stanford Cardinal football|Stanford Cardinal]] and was selected by the [[Indianapolis Colts]] in the third round of the [[2019 NFL draft]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=April 24, 2019 |title=Meet the Bay Area NFL Draft Prospects: Stanford Linebacker Bobby Okereke |url=https://abc7news.com/5266451/ |access-date=December 25, 2019 |website=ABC7 San Francisco |language=en}}</ref>

==Early life==
Okereke was born in [[Santa Ana, California]] to parents who emigrated from Nigeria.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Stankevitz |first=JJ |date=September 28, 2021 |title=It's Pronounced 'Oh-ker-uh-KAY:' Why Colts' LB Bobby Okereke Is Taking Ownership Of Cultural, Correct Pronunciation Of His Last Name |url=https://www.colts.com/news/bobby-okereke-correct-pronunciation-last-name-nigeria-linebacker |access-date=May 18, 2023 |website=Colts.com}}</ref> At age 16, he became an [[Eagle Scout]] with Troop 243.<ref>{{cite new|newspaper=Orange County Register|title=Okereke joins the rank of Eagle Scouts|url=https://www.ocregister.com/2013/07/05/okereke-joins-the-rank-of-eagle-scouts/|date=July 5, 2013|access-date=January 17, 2026}}</ref> He attended and played [[high school football]] at [[Foothill High School (Orange County, California)|Foothill High School]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Bobby Okereke's High School Timeline |url=https://www.maxpreps.com/athlete/bobby-okereke/_1N-A_TtEeKZ5AAmVebBJg/default.htm |access-date=December 25, 2019 |website=MaxPreps.com |language=en}}</ref>

==College career==
Okereke attended and played [[college football]] at [[Stanford University]]. He redshirted as a freshman in 2014.<ref>{{Cite web |date=August 19, 2015 |title=Stanford offensive line looks ready to live up to billing |url=https://www.sfchronicle.com/collegesports/article/Stanford-offensive-line-looks-ready-to-live-up-to-6452133.php |access-date=December 25, 2019 |website=SFChronicle.com |language=en-US}}</ref> He contributed on the field from 2015 to 2018. He recorded 227 total tackles (20.0 were for loss), 10.5 sacks, one interception (a 52-yard pick-six), eight passes defensed, one fumble recovery, and three forced fumbles.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Bobby Okereke College Stats, School, Draft, Gamelog, Splits |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/players/bobby-okereke-1.html |access-date=December 25, 2019 |website=College Football at Sports-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> He was named [[Pac-12]] Honorable Mention in 2017<ref>{{Cite web |date=December 5, 2017 |title=Pac-12 Football All-Conference Team Announced |url=https://pac-12.com/news/2017/12/5/pac-12-football-all-conference-team-announced.aspx |access-date=November 3, 2023 |website=Pac-12}}</ref> and 2018.<ref>{{Cite web |date=December 4, 2018 |title=Pac-12 Football All-Conference honors announced |url=https://pac-12.com/article/2018/12/03/pac-12-football-all-conference-honors-announced |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181205103345/https://pac-12.com/article/2018/12/03/pac-12-football-all-conference-honors-announced |url-status=dead |archive-date=December 5, 2018 |access-date=November 3, 2023 |website=Pac-12}}</ref>

===Indianapolis Colts===
Okereke was selected by the [[Indianapolis Colts]] in the third round (89th overall) of the [[2019 NFL draft]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Walker |first=Andrew |date=April 26, 2019 |title=Colts Select Linebacker Bobby Okereke With 89th-Overall Pick |url=https://www.colts.com/news/colts-select-linebacker-bobby-okereke-with-89th-overall-pick |access-date=November 3, 2023 |website=Colts.com}}</ref> The pick was announced by former Colts punter [[Pat McAfee]]. He made his NFL debut in the season opener against the [[Los Angeles Chargers]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Indianapolis Colts at Los Angeles Chargers - September 8th, 2019 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201909080sdg.htm |access-date=December 25, 2019 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> He earned his first career start in Week 3 against the [[Atlanta Falcons]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Colts' Bobby Okereke: Drawing start Sunday |url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/football/news/colts-bobby-okereke-drawing-start-sunday/ |access-date=December 25, 2019 |website=CBSSports.com |date=September 22, 2019 |language=en}}</ref> In Week 13 against the [[Tennessee Titans]], Okereke recorded a strip sack on [[Ryan Tannehill]] which was recovered by teammate [[Justin Houston]] in the 31–17 loss. This was Okereke's first career sack in the NFL.<ref>{{Cite web |date=December 1, 2019 |title=Blocked field goal helps Titans turn table with win at Indy |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/recap?gameId=401128058 |access-date=December 1, 2019 |website=[[ESPN]] |agency=Associated Press}}</ref> In the 2019 season, he recorded one sack, 65 total tackles, two passes defended, and two forced fumbles.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Bobby Okereke 2019 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/O/OkerBo00/gamelog/2019/ |access-date=November 3, 2023 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

In Week 5 of the 2020 season against the [[Cleveland Browns]], Okereke recorded his first career interception off a pass thrown by [[Baker Mayfield]] during the 32–23 loss.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Indianapolis Colts at Cleveland Browns - October 11th, 2020 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202010110cle.htm |access-date=October 11, 2020 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> In the 2020 season, he recorded 72 total tackles, one interception, and six passes defended.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Bobby Okereke 2020 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/O/OkerBo00/gamelog/2020/ |access-date=November 3, 2023 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

In the 2021 season, Okereke started in all 17 games. He finished with one sack, 132 total tackles, two interceptions, and four passes defended.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Bobby Okereke 2021 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/O/OkerBo00/gamelog/2021/ |access-date=November 3, 2023 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

In the 2022 season, Okereke started in all 17 games. He finished with 151 total tackles, five passes defended, and two forced fumbles.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Bobby Okereke 2022 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/O/OkerBo00/gamelog/2022/ |access-date=November 3, 2023 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

===New York Giants===
On March 16, 2023, Okereke signed a four-year contract with the [[New York Giants]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Eisen |first=Michael |date=March 16, 2023 |title=LB Bobby Okereke excited to be 'part of the rise' |url=https://www.giants.com/news/bobby-okereke-contract-nfl-free-agency-2023-wink-martindale-indianapolis-colts |access-date=November 3, 2023 |website=Giants.com}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|work=SI.com|url=https://www.si.com/college/stanford/pros/bobby-okereke-agrees-to-deal-with-new-york-giants|title=Bobby Okereke agrees to deal with New York Giants|first=Kevin|last=Borba|date=March 15, 2023|accessdate=March 16, 2023}}</ref> In the [[2023 NFL season]], he recorded 149 total tackles, 11 tackles for loss, 2.5 sacks, 4 forced fumbles, 2 interceptions, and 10 passes defensed.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Bobby Okereke 2023 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/O/OkerBo00/gamelog/2023/ |access-date=2024-09-13 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> Okereke, along with teammate [[Xavier McKinney]], were the only defenders in the NFL to not miss a snap in the entire season.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Leonard |first=Pat |date=2024-01-05 |title=Giants’ Bobby Okereke, Xavier McKinney only two NFL defenders who have played 100% of snaps entering Week 18 |url=https://www.nydailynews.com/2024/01/05/giants-bobby-okereke-xavier-mckinney-only-two-nfl-defenders-who-have-played-100-of-snaps-entering-week-18/ |access-date=2024-02-09 |website=New York Daily News |language=en-US}}</ref> In the 2024 season, he had two sacks, 93 tackles, three passes defended, three forced fumbles, and two fumble recoveries.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Bobby Okereke 2024 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/O/OkerBo00/gamelog/2024/ |access-date=2025-02-03 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref>

During Week 18 of the 2025 season, Okereke was named the NFC Defensive Player of the Week for his two turnovers that lead to 10 points and a 34–17 Giants win over the [[2025 Dallas Cowboys season|Dallas Cowboys]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Valentine |first=Ed |date=January 7, 2026 |title=NY Giants linebacker Bobby Okereke named NFC Player of the Week |url=https://www.bigblueview.com/new-york-giants-news/151414/linebacker-bobby-okereke-named-nfc-player-of-the-week-for-week-18 |access-date=January 9, 2026 |website=Big Blue View |language=en-US}}</ref> Okereke finished 2025 with a team-leading 143 tackles.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Bobby Okereke 2025 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/O/OkerBo00/gamelog/2025/ |access-date=2026-03-31 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> On March 4, 2026, Okereke was released by the Giants.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Salamone |first1=Dan |date=March 5, 2026 |title=Giants release former captain Bobby Okereke |url=https://www.giants.com/news/giants-release-former-captain-bobby-okereke-linebacker |access-date=5 March 2026 |website=giants.com}}</ref>
