== Controversies ==
Okereke was the subject of a [[sexual assault]] investigation at Stanford in 2015. Three members of the university's five-person investigative panel concluded Okereke committed sexual assault, but the ruling didn't cross the 4-1 threshold necessary to pursue further punitive action.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Shapiro |first1=Michael |title=Colts Were Aware of 2015 Sexual Assault Accusation Before Drafting Bobby Okereke |url=https://www.si.com/nfl/2019/06/05/bobby-okereke-colts-draft-sexual-assault-claim-stanford-linebacker |website=SI |date=June 5, 2019 |access-date=December 8, 2020}}</ref> Okereke has maintained that the allegations are untrue.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Abdeldaiem |first1=Alaa |title=Colts' Bobby Okereke Calls 2015 Sexual Assault Allegations 'Untrue' |url=https://www.si.com/nfl/2019/07/28/bobby-okereke-sexual-assault-allegations-untrue-colts |website=SI |date=July 28, 2019 |access-date=December 8, 2020}}</ref>

'''Carlos''' "'''Boogie'''" '''Basham Jr.''' (born December 16, 1997) is an American professional [[American football|football]] [[linebacker]] for the [[DC Defenders]] of the [[United Football League (2024–present)|United Football League]] (UFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Wake Forest Demon Deacons football|Wake Forest Demon Deacons]], and was selected by the [[Buffalo Bills]] in the second round of the [[2021 NFL draft]].

==Early life==
Basham attended [[Northside High School (Roanoke, Virginia)|Northside]] in [[Roanoke, Virginia]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Anderson |first=Robert |date=November 27, 2014 |title=Northside's 'Boogie' Basham dances to recruiting rhythm |url=https://www.roanoke.com/sports/high_schools/northside-s-boogie-basham-dances-to-recruiting-rhythm/article_e087853e-99cb-5143-83bb-bbbaeb4d773a.html |access-date=May 19, 2023 |website=Roanoke Times}}</ref>  As a senior, he had 76 tackles and seven sacks. He committed to [[Wake Forest University]] to play [[college football]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Appicello |first=John |date=July 7, 2015 |title=Carlos Basham Jr. headed to Wake Forest |url=https://www.wsls.com/sports/2015/07/07/carlos-basham-jr-headed-to-wake-forest/ |access-date=October 10, 2023 |website=WSLS}}</ref>

==College career==
After redshirting his first year at Wake Forest in 2016, Basham played in all 13 games in 2017 and had 24 tackles. As a junior in 2018, he had 64 tackles and 4.5 sacks.<ref>{{Cite web |last=O'Neill |first=Conor |date=March 7, 2019 |title=Boogie Basham is now Wake Forest's most-experienced defensive lineman — and is elevating game to match what comes with that |url=https://www.journalnow.com/sports/college/wfu/boogie-basham-is-now-wake-forest-s-most-experienced-defensive/article_d44ec23d-0fb5-5510-b331-294d3183fde0.html |access-date=October 10, 2023 |website=Winston-Salem Journal}}</ref> Basham returned to Wake Forest as a starter in 2019.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Doughty |first=Doug |date=October 23, 2019 |title=Doughty College Notebook: Former Viking Basham hitting stride at Wake Forest |url=https://www.roanoke.com/sports/college/doughty-college-notebook-former-viking-basham-hitting-stride-at-wake/article_8bfef904-cd28-59d0-9799-1bdad40fa8c4.html |access-date=October 10, 2023 |website=Roanoke Times}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=December 2, 2019 |title=One timeline for NFL decision |url=https://www.journalnow.com/sports/college/wfu/one-timeline-for-nfl-decision/article_d5b18bdc-651d-5153-ba5d-120ff45c8f60.html |access-date=October 10, 2023 |website=Winston-Salem Journal}}</ref> On December 21, 2019, Basham announced that he would resume his college stint for his senior season in 2020.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Taylor |first=John |date=December 21, 2019 |title=DE Carlos Basham will return to Wake Forest for senior season |url=https://www.nbcsports.com/college-football/news/carlos-basham-wake-forest-2020-nfl-draft |access-date=October 10, 2023 |website=NBC Sports |language=en-US}}</ref>

=== Buffalo Bills ===
Basham was selected by the [[Buffalo Bills]] in the second round (61st overall) of the [[2021 NFL draft]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=LaBarber |first=Jourdon |date=April 30, 2021 |title=5 things to know about defensive end Boogie Basham |url=https://www.buffalobills.com/news/carlos-basham-nfl-draft-defensive-end-wake-forest |access-date=May 8, 2021 |website=BuffaloBills.com}}</ref> On May 12, 2021, Basham officially signed with the Bills.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Robinson |first=Sam |date=May 12, 2021 |title=Bills Sign Round 2 Pick Carlos Basham Jr. |url=https://www.profootballrumors.com/2021/05/bills-sign-second-round-pick-carlos-basham-jr |access-date=October 10, 2023 |website=Pro Football Rumors |language=en-US}}</ref> As a rookie, he appeared in eight games. He finished with 2.5 sacks and 18 total tackles.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Boogie Basham 2021 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/B/BashCa00/gamelog/2021/ |access-date=November 13, 2024 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

On September 8, 2022, during the kickoff game at the [[Los Angeles Rams]], Basham recorded his first career interception, a 21 yard pick from [[Matthew Stafford]].<ref name="e287">{{cite web | last=Knoblauch | first=Austin | title=Matthew Stafford throws three picks, sacked seven times in Rams' blowout loss | website=Los Angeles Times | date=September 9, 2022 | url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/rams/liveblog/rams-buffalo-bills-live-updates-blog-start-time-score-nfl-news | access-date=November 13, 2024}}</ref> This interception helped seal the game for the Bills as they won 31–10. Basham also recorded a sack on Stafford earlier in the night.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Buffalo Bills at Los Angeles Rams - September 8th, 2022 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202209080ram.htm |access-date=October 10, 2023 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> In the 2022 season, he appeared in 15 games and finished with two sacks, 19 total tackles, one interception, two passes defended, and one fumble recovery.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Boogie Basham 2022 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/B/BashCa00/gamelog/2022/ |access-date=November 13, 2024 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> He recorded a sack in the Bills' Wild Card Round win over the Miami Dolphins.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Wild Card - Miami Dolphins at Buffalo Bills - January 15th, 2023 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202301150buf.htm |access-date=November 13, 2024 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

=== New York Giants ===
On August 29, 2023, Basham was traded to the [[New York Giants]], along with 2025 seventh-round pick (Korie Black), in exchange for a 2025 sixth-round pick (Dorian Strong) .<ref>{{Cite web |last=Eisen |first=Michael |date=August 30, 2023 |title=Giants acquire OLB Boogie Basham in trade with Bills |url=https://www.giants.com/news/boogie-basham-trade-details-buffalo-bills-roster-2023-nfl-isaiah-simmons |access-date=September 6, 2023 |website=Giants.com |language=en-US}}</ref> He appeared in 13 games in the 2023 season.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Boogie Basham 2023 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/B/BashCa00/gamelog/2023/ |access-date=November 13, 2024 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

On October 22, 2024, Basham was waived by the Giants and re-signed to the practice squad.<ref name="l150">{{cite web | last=Eisen | first=Michael | title=Giants sign DT Armon Watts off practice squad; OLB Boogie Basham waived | website=Giants.com| date=October 22, 2024 | url=https://www.giants.com/news/giants-sign-dt-armon-watts-off-practice-squad-olb-boogie-basham-waived | access-date=November 13, 2024}}</ref>

===Carolina Panthers===
On January 21, 2025, Basham signed a reserve/future contract with the [[Carolina Panthers]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Panthers add two more to future contracts|url=https://www.panthers.com/news/panthers-add-two-more-to-future-contracts-boogie-basham-james-mitchell|author=Gantt, Darin|website=Panthers.com|date=January 21, 2025}}</ref> He was released on August 26, and re-signed to the practice squad.<ref>{{cite web|title=Panthers make moves to get to the 53-man roster|url=https://www.panthers.com/news/panthers-make-moves-to-get-to-the-53-man-roster|author=Gantt, Darin|website=Panthers.com|date=August 26, 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Panthers add 13 players to practice squad|url=https://www.panthers.com/news/panthers-add-13-players-to-practice-squad|author=Gantt, Darin|website=Panthers.com|date=August 27, 2025}}</ref> On October 18, Basham was elevated from the practice squad for Carolina's Week 7 game against the [[2025 New York Jets season|New York Jets]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Panthers activate two from injured reserve, place one on IR|url=https://www.panthers.com/news/panthers-activate-two-from-injured-reserve-place-one-on-ir-jalen-coker-austin-corbett-patrick-jones-ii|access-date=October 24, 2025|website=panthers.com|language=en}}</ref> He was released on November 4.<ref>{{cite web|title=Panthers make practice squad moves, return three, on Tuesday|url=https://www.panthers.com/news/panthers-make-practice-squad-moves-return-three-on-tuesday|author=Hill, Kassidy|website=Panthers.com|date=November 4, 2025}}</ref>

===Las Vegas Raiders===
On November 25, 2025, Basham was signed to the [[Las Vegas Raiders]]' practice squad.<ref>{{cite web|title=Raiders sign DL Boogie Basham to the practice squad|url=https://www.raiders.com/news/raiders-sign-dl-boogie-basham-to-the-practice-squad-2025-transactions|website=Raiders.com|date=November 25, 2025}}</ref>

=== DC Defenders ===
On March 12, 2026, Basham signed with the [[DC Defenders]] of the [[United Football League (2024–present)|United Football League]] (UFL).<ref>{{cite web |last1=Larsen |first1=James |title=Defenders Add Boogie Basham, Battlehawks Re-Sign Gary Jennings |url=https://pfnewsroom.com/news/defenders-add-boogie-basham-battlehawks-re-sign-gary-jennings/ |website=PF Newsroom |access-date=14 March 2026}}</ref>

'''Bobby Miguel Price''' (born April 25, 1998) is an American professional [[American football|football]] [[cornerback]] for the [[Dallas Renegades]] of the [[United Football League (2024)|United Football League]] (UFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Norfolk State Spartans football|Norfolk State Spartans]] and signed with the [[Detroit Lions]] as an [[undrafted free agent]] in 2020. Price has also played for the [[Arizona Cardinals]] and [[Washington Commanders]].

==College career==
Price was born in [[Virginia Beach, Virginia]], and is of [[Puerto Rican people|Puerto Rican]] descent.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.azcardinals.com/news/bj-ojulari-representing-not-only-cardinals-but-nigeria|title=BJ Ojulari Representing Not Only Cardinals, But Nigeria|website=www.azcardinals.com}}</ref> He played [[college football]] at [[Norfolk State Spartans football|Norfolk State]]. During his freshman season, he played in nine games, and started four games at free safety. During his sophomore season, he started in all 11 games and ranked fourth on the team, and tied for 18th in the [[Mid-Eastern Athletic Conference]] (MEAC) with 69 tackles. During his junior season, he started all 10 games he played and ranked fourth on the team with 59 tackles. He also posted 2.5 tackles-for-loss, two interceptions, deflected eight passes, recovered two fumbles, and tied for fourth in the MEAC with 10 passes defended. Following the season he earned All-MEAC third-team honors.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://hbcusports.com/2018/11/26/meac-releases-2018-football-postseason-honors-teams/ |title=MEAC releases 2018 football postseason honors, teams |website=[[:simple:HBCU Sports|HBCU Sports]] |date=November 26, 2018 |access-date=December 6, 2020}}</ref> Price also participated with the NSU track and field team in the spring, where he placed fourth in the long jump at the MEAC indoor championships in February, and won the MEAC outdoor long jump championship, with a personal-best jump of 25 feet, 10.25 inches.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://nsuspartans.com/news/2019/5/3/mens-track-price-soars-to-long-jump-title-at-meac-outdoor-championships.aspx |title=Price Soars to Long Jump Title at MEAC Outdoor Championships |website=nsuspartans.com |date=May 3, 2019 |access-date=December 6, 2020}}</ref>

During his senior season, he started all 12 games at strong safety and finished the season with 73 tackles, including 2.5 tackles-for-loss, eight pass breakups, recovered two fumbles, and returned his lone interception 84-yards for a touchdown. He ranked 16th in the MEAC in tackles, 10th in passes defended and tied for third in fumble recoveries.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://nsuspartans.com/sports/football/roster/bobby-price/5007 |title=Bobby Price bio |website=nsuspartans.com |access-date=December 6, 2020}}</ref> Following the season he earned All-MEAC second-team honors.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://hbcusports.com/2019/11/26/meac-releases-2019-all-conference-teams-postseason-honors/ |title=MEAC releases 2019 all-conference teams, postseason honors |website=[[:simple:HBCU Sports|HBCU Sports]] |date=November 26, 2019 |access-date=December 6, 2020}}</ref> Price finished his career with 229 tackles, eight for loss, seven interceptions, 23 pass breakups and four fumble recoveries.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://hbcusports.com/2020/04/25/norfolk-states-bobby-price-agrees-to-nfl-free-agent-deal-with-detroit-lions/ |title=Norfolk State's Bobby Price agrees to NFL free agent deal with Detroit Lions |website=HBCU Sports |date=April 25, 2020 |access-date=December 6, 2020}}</ref>

===Detroit Lions===
Price signed with the [[Detroit Lions]] as an [[undrafted free agent]] on May 1, 2020.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.detroitnews.com/story/sports/nfl/lions/2020/04/28/detroit-lions-announce-agreement-seven-undrafted-free-agents/3041657001/ |title=Lions announce agreement with seven undrafted free agents |newspaper=The Detroit News |date=April 28, 2020 |access-date=December 6, 2020}}</ref> He was waived during final roster cuts on September 5, 2020,<ref>{{cite news |title=Lions announce roster moves |url=https://www.detroitlions.com/news/lions-announce-roster-moves-x4330 |website=DetroitLions.com |date=September 5, 2020 |access-date=January 13, 2021}}</ref> and signed to the team's [[practice squad]] the next day.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://nsuspartans.com/news/2020/9/7/football-price-signed-to-detroit-lions-practice-squad.aspx |title=Price Signed to Detroit Lions Practice Squad |website=nsuspartans.com |date=September 7, 2020 |access-date=December 6, 2020}}</ref> He was elevated to the active roster on December 5 and December 12 for the team's weeks 13 and 14 games against the [[Chicago Bears]] and [[Green Bay Packers]], and reverted to the practice squad after each game.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.wavy.com/news/local-news/former-nsu-player-and-virginia-beach-native-bobby-price-elevated-to-lions-53-man-roster/ |title=Former NSU player and Virginia Beach native Bobby Price elevated to Lions 53-man roster |website=wavy.com |first=Brian |last=Parsons |date=December 5, 2020 |access-date=December 5, 2020}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.mlive.com/lions/2020/12/hunter-bryant-among-2-udfas-headed-for-nfl-debut-under-darrell-bevell-dandre-swift-out.html |title=Hunter Bryant among 2 UDFAs headed for NFL debut under Darrell Bevell; D'Andre Swift out |website=MLive.com |first=Kyle |last=Meinke |date=December 6, 2020 |access-date=December 6, 2020}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |author=Williams, Charean |title=Everson Griffen placed on COVID-19 list |url=https://profootballtalk.nbcsports.com/2020/12/12/everson-griffen-placed-on-covid-19-list/ |website=NBCSports.com |date=December 12, 2020 |access-date=January 27, 2021}}</ref> On January 2, 2021, Price was promoted to the active roster.<ref>{{cite web|title=Lions announce roster moves|url=https://www.detroitlions.com/news/lions-announce-roster-moves-x9588|website=DetroitLions.com|date=January 2, 2021}}</ref> On October 22, 2022, Price was placed on [[injured reserve]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Detroit Lions place DJ Chark, Bobby Price on injured reserve|url=https://www.prideofdetroit.com/2022/10/22/23412728/detroit-lions-dj-chark-bobby-price-injured-reserve-2022|work=Pride of Detroit|publisher=SB Nation|date=October 22, 2022}}</ref>

===Arizona Cardinals===
On June 5, 2023, Price signed with the [[Arizona Cardinals]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Cardinals sign Dylan Mabin, Bobby Price|url=https://profootballtalk.nbcsports.com/2023/06/05/cardinals-sign-dylan-mabin-bobby-price/amp/|work=Pro Football Talk|publisher=NBCSports.com|date=June 5, 2023|access-date=June 6, 2023|archive-date=June 6, 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230606225355/https://profootballtalk.nbcsports.com/2023/06/05/cardinals-sign-dylan-mabin-bobby-price/amp/|url-status=dead}}</ref> He was waived on August 29, 2023, and re-signed to the practice squad.<ref>{{cite web|title= Cardinals Make Moves To Get To 53-Man Roster|url=https://www.azcardinals.com/news/arizona-cardinals-make-moves-to-get-to-53-man-roster|website=AZCardinals.com|date=August 29, 2023}}</ref> On October 26, 2023, Price was signed to the active roster.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Root |first1=Jess |title=Cardinals sign CB Bobby Price to 53-man roster |url=https://cardswire.usatoday.com/2023/10/26/cardinals-sign-cb-bobby-price-to-53-man-roster/ |website=Cardinals Wire |access-date=27 October 2023}}</ref> He was placed on injured reserve on November 7, 2023.<ref>{{cite web|title=Cardinals Activate Kyler Murray From PUP List|url=https://www.azcardinals.com/news/cardinals-activate-kyler-murray-from-pup-list|author=Urban, Darren|website=AZCardinals.com|date=November 7, 2023}}</ref> He was activated on December 30, 2023. On August 27, 2024, he was waived by the Cardinals as part of final roster cuts before the start of the 2024 season.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.azcardinals.com/news/cardinals-trim-roster-to-get-to-53-for-2024-regular-season|work=AZCardinals.com|title=Cardinals Trim Roster To Get To 53 For Regular Season|date=August 27, 2024|accessdate=August 27, 2024|first=Darren|last=Urban}}</ref>

On August 28, 2024, Price signed with the [[Washington Commanders]]' practice squad.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://commanderswire.usatoday.com/2024/08/29/commanders-sign-16-players-to-practice-squad/|work=USAToday.com|title=Commanders sign 16 players to practice squad|first=Bryan|last=Manning|date=August 29, 2024|accessdate=August 29, 2024}}</ref> He re-signed with the team on February 10, 2025, and was released on August 26.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Alper |first1=Josh |title=Commanders sign CB Bobby Price |url=https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/profootballtalk/rumor-mill/news/commanders-sign-cb-bobby-price |website=Pro Football Talk |access-date=10 February 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last1=Zelby |first1=Zach |title=Commanders place Sam Cosmi on Reserve/PUP list; release 30 players |url=https://www.commanders.com/news/commanders-place-sam-cosmi-on-reserve-pup-list-release-30-players |website=Commanders.com |access-date=August 27, 2025 |date=August 26, 2025}}</ref>

'''Robert Lee Neely''' (born March 22, 1974) is an American actor and former [[American football]] [[tight end]] who played for the [[Chicago Bears]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] at [[University of Virginia|Virginia University]].

== Early life and education ==
Neely played all four of his college years at [[University of Virginia|Virginia University]]. He played his first year at Virginia, being one of only four true freshman that season. After his first season at the University of Virginia, he was regarded as one of the best freshman Tight-Ends in the country. After suffering, a high ankle sprain during a career high statistical game against the University of Michigan in 1995, Bobby played in only five games his senior season. He was very frustrated that he had missed the chance to be an All-ACC tight end. He believed that he deserved the award because he did just as well as the winner. He also claimed that he was the best tight end out there and one of the only 'real' ones.<ref name="Cav hopes to grab lost glory">{{cite news |date=December 27, 1995 |title=Cav hopes to grab lost glory |newspaper=[[Daily Press (Virginia)]] |url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/103924814/daily-press/}} {{Open access}}</ref><ref name="Cav hopes to grab lost glory: continued">{{cite news |date=December 27, 1995 |title=Cav hopes to grab lost glory: continued |newspaper=[[Daily Press (Virginia)]] |url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/103924833/daily-press/}} {{Open access}}</ref> Meaning, having the ability to both block and catch passes was key. While there, he caught 50 passes for 509 yards.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/players/bobby-neely-1.html |title=Bobby Neely college statistics |access-date=June 10, 2022 |website=College Football at Sports-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> Unfortunately out of those 50 catches, none resulted in a touchdown. Some believe these factors led to him being undrafted.

== Professional career ==
After college, he was signed to the [[Chicago Bears]] as an undrafted free agent. He did not make the final roster. Therefore, he decided to sign with the [[Miami Dolphins]] practice squad. About five games into the season, however, the Bears had lost all of their active tight ends due to injuries. They re-signed Neely to their active roster where he was now the starting tight end.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/103924583/northwest-herald/|newspaper=[[Northwest Herald]]|via=[[Newspapers.com]]|title=Neely goes from fodder to starter|date=November 8, 1996}} {{Open access}}</ref> During his rookie season, he played in eleven games, starting in five. He caught 9-of-13 passes for 92 yards in the games he played.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/N/NeelBo20.htm | title=Bobby Neely NFL statistics |access-date=June 10, 2022 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com}}</ref> He suffered a career-ending injury before his second season.

== Post career ==
Neely took his talents to Los Angeles to pursue a career in entertainment. He has appeared on shows ''[[NCIS (TV series)|NCIS]]'', ''[[Grey's Anatomy]]'', and most recently ''[[Rebel (2021 TV series)|Rebel]]'', and ''Seal Team''. He currently still lives in Los Angeles and is a Luxury Real Estate agent with Amalfi Estates in Pacific Palisades.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.rottentomatoes.com/celebrity/bobby_neely | title=Bobby Neely Rotten Tomatoes profile |access-date=June 15, 2022 |website=RottenTomatoes.com}}</ref>
